import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyH1Locus

/-!
# CHART-U(b) — datum-level openness of the chart-membership (witness) locus
(`informal/w4-datb-worksheet.md` §1.6, `informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md` §3.3)

The affine-level heart of the shared CHART-U(b) brick, stated directly on a pinned
basic-open cocycle datum in the **witness form** the `chartLocus` predicate uses.

For a datum `D` over an affine base `B`, the locus of primes `q` of `B` at which the
fibre class of `D` at `κ(q)` admits an effective witness divisor with vanishing `H¹`
is Zariski-open in `Spec B`.  This is the single sanctioned openness mechanism of the
campaign (`datumRigidEngine_isOpen_vanishing`, Noetherian-free — dat-d §3.5) read
through the two-way datum dictionary of C1
(`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness`,
`informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md` GAP-6): the engine open is the complex-form fibre
condition `Subsingleton (H¹(pair D) ⊗[B] κ(q))`, and the dictionary rewrites it,
pointwise and class-intrinsically, as the effective-witness/h¹-vanishing condition.

Role in the CHART-U(b) chain (the two unlanded links of §5 risk 1):

* **the shifted-datum constructor (link 1):** over the étale carrier `B` the plus
  class collapses to an honest Čech class; twisted by the theta layer and DAT-C's
  GAP-1 inverse datum into the `λθᵐ(Σ-shift)⁻¹` class, then extracted
  (`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq`) to a datum `D`.  The output of
  that link is exactly a `BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π` — the input of the theorem
  below, whose witness set is then the `chartLocus`-over-`B`.
* **the étale-image openness transport (link 2):** the locus over the test base `A`
  is the image, under the (open, surjective) étale carrier map `Spec B → Spec A`, of
  the open locus this theorem produces — carried to `A` by mathlib's
  `IsOpenMap.isQuotientMap`/`IsQuotientMap.isOpen_preimage` once the fibre-field
  invariance identifies the preimage.

The theorem is class-intrinsic (any datum in the class has the same witness set, by
(V1a)), so a change of extracted representative is free.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

/-- **CHART-U(b), the datum-level witness-locus openness** (`w4-datc` §3.3 step (3)):
for a pinned basic-open cocycle datum `D` over the affine base `B`, the locus of primes
`q` at which the fibre class of `D` at `κ(q)` has an effective witness divisor with
vanishing `H¹` is open in `Spec B`.

This is `datumRigidEngine_isOpen_vanishing` (the single audited openness engine,
Noetherian-free) read in the class/witness form of the `chartLocus` predicate through
the two-way datum dictionary
`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness` (C1, GAP-6):
pointwise the engine's complex-form condition `Subsingleton (H¹(pair D) ⊗[B] κ(q))`
is exactly the existence of such a witness. -/
theorem BasicOpenCocycleDatum.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing
    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) :
    IsOpen {q : PrimeSpectrum B |
      ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left).CurveDivisor,
        Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass q.asIdeal.ResidueField W
            = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B q.asIdeal.ResidueField) D.cechPicClass
          ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
              ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left.divisorSheaf
                q.asIdeal.ResidueField W) 1)} := by
  have hset : {q : PrimeSpectrum B |
      ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left).CurveDivisor,
        Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass q.asIdeal.ResidueField W
            = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B q.asIdeal.ResidueField) D.cechPicClass
          ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
              ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left.divisorSheaf
                q.asIdeal.ResidueField W) 1)}
      = {p : PrimeSpectrum B |
          Subsingleton ((datumPair D).H1 ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField)} := by
    refine Set.ext fun q => ?_
    exact (D.subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness q.asIdeal.ResidueField).symm
  rw [hset]
  exact datumRigidEngine_isOpen_vanishing D hπ

/-! ## The openness transport (CHART-U(b) link 2, topological half)

The engine produces the open witness locus over the étale carrier `Spec B` (or, on the
away pieces, over `Spec (Localization.Away f)`).  CHART-U(b)'s transport (ii)
(`w4-datb` §1.6, "the Kleiman tex 2204-2244 step, now one `IsOpenMap` application")
carries it down to the test base `Spec A` along the étale carrier map, which is open
and surjective.  The pure-topology core of that step is below; the remaining
mathematical content of link 2 is the *fibre-field invariance* that identifies the
preimage of the base locus with the carrier locus (`κ(q)/κ(p)` a separable extension;
`isH1VanishingAt_comap_away_iff` is the landed avatar for the away case). -/

/-- **Openness descends along an open continuous surjection**: if `f` is continuous,
open, and surjective and `f ⁻¹' V` is open, then `V` is open — because
`V = f '' (f ⁻¹' V)` (surjectivity) and `f` carries opens to opens.  This is the
topological core of CHART-U(b)'s transport (ii). -/
theorem isOpen_of_isOpen_preimage_of_isOpenMap_surjective
    {X Y : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] {f : X → Y}
    (hcont : Continuous f) (hopen : IsOpenMap f) (hsurj : Function.Surjective f)
    {V : Set Y} (hV : IsOpen (f ⁻¹' V)) : IsOpen V :=
  ((hopen.isQuotientMap hcont hsurj).isOpen_preimage).mp hV

/-- **The `Spec`-level openness transport of CHART-U(b)** (transport (ii), topological
half): for a ring map `f : R →+* S` whose induced `Spec S → Spec R` is open and
surjective (e.g. an étale carrier map), a locus of `Spec R` whose preimage in `Spec S`
is open is itself open.  The engine's open witness locus lives on the carrier `Spec S`;
this pushes it to the test base `Spec R`. -/
theorem isOpen_of_isOpen_comap_preimage {R S : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S]
    (f : R →+* S) (hopen : IsOpenMap (PrimeSpectrum.comap f))
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap f))
    {V : Set (PrimeSpectrum R)} (hV : IsOpen (PrimeSpectrum.comap f ⁻¹' V)) :
    IsOpen V :=
  isOpen_of_isOpen_preimage_of_isOpenMap_surjective
    (PrimeSpectrum.continuous_comap f) hopen hsurj hV

end AlgebraicGeometry

/-! ## The spelling bridge (`I-0144`) -/

/-- **The two `overSpecMap`s agree at a residue field.**

`overSpecMap B κ(p)` (`Cohomology/RelativeSectionsLinear.lean:147`) is built from the
`algebraMap`; `Over.overSpecMap φ` (`Picard/RelPicAlgebra.lean:44`) from an arbitrary
`k`-algebra map.  These are two independent definitions of the same morphism in different
namespaces — the duplicate pair filed as `I-0144` — and at the canonical map
`(Algebra.ofId B κ(p)).restrictScalars k` they are definitionally equal.

Stated because the engine's base-change lemmas live on the first spelling and the degree seam
on the second, so no composition of the two is possible without it. -/
theorem relCurveMap_eq_whiskerLeft_residueField (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (p : PrimeSpectrum B) :
    relCurveMap C B p.asIdeal.ResidueField
      = (C ◁ Over.overSpecMap
          ((Algebra.ofId B p.asIdeal.ResidueField).restrictScalars k)).left :=
  rfl

/-! ## The datum in the presentation binder is not a real constraint -/

/-- **Every relative Picard class over a test ring is presented by a cocycle datum.**

`relPicMk` is surjective (`RelPic.lean:75`) and `exists_cechPicClass_eq`
(`Cohomology/GluedSheafExtraction.lean:301`) turns the resulting Čech class into a
`BasicOpenCocycleDatum` with the same class, at **every** `k`-algebra `B`.

This is what makes the presentation binder of the theorems below a condition on the *class*
rather than on a choice of datum: a `pic⁰` class that is `PicEtAff.unit` of some relative class
at all is presented by some datum, and `exists_datum_pic0_presentation` extracts it. -/
theorem exists_datum_relPicMk_eq (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π]
    (z : relPic C (overSpec k B)) :
    ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π, relPicMk C (overSpec k B) D.cechPicClass = z := by
  obtain ⟨L, hL⟩ := relPicMk_surjective C (overSpec k B) z
  obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ := BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq (π := π) L
  exact ⟨D, by rw [hD, hL]⟩

/-- **The presentation binder, in its weakest form**: if the affine collapse of `lam` is
`PicEtAff.unit` of *any* relative class, then it is `PicEtAff.unit` of `relPicMk` of some
datum's Čech class — which is the hypothesis the theorems below take.

So those theorems do not secretly quantify over a lucky datum: the datum is produced, and the
surviving hypothesis is the `picEtAffineEquiv`/`unit` seam on `lam` alone. -/
theorem exists_datum_pic0_presentation (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π]
    (lam : picEt C (overSpec k B))
    (h : ∃ z : relPic C (overSpec k B), picEtAffineEquiv C B lam = PicEtAff.unit C B z) :
    ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π,
      picEtAffineEquiv C B lam
        = PicEtAff.unit C B (relPicMk C (overSpec k B) D.cechPicClass) := by
  obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := h
  obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ := exists_datum_relPicMk_eq C B π z
  exact ⟨D, by rw [hz, hD]⟩

namespace BasicOpenCocycleDatum

/-! ## The fibrewise binder, discharged -/

/-- **THE DISCHARGE**: the engine's fibrewise binder holds for a cocycle-presented `pic⁰`
class, at genus `0`.

Composition of three landed steps and the bridge above:
`cechPicClass_baseChange` moves the fibre class onto `Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap …)`;
the bridge rewrites that as the whiskering the degree seam speaks about;
`classDeg_fibre_eq_zero_of_cocyclePresented` gives `classDeg κ(p) = 0` from the membership;
and the engine's `fibre_cechPicClass_eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero` converts degree `0` to
triviality at genus `0`.

The five fibre instances are installed by hand — they do not synthesize through the `relCurve`
`def` barrier, exactly as `Pic0RingDatumEngine` records. -/
theorem htriv_of_pic0 (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) (hg : genus C = 0)
    (lam : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k B))
    (h : picEtAffineEquiv C B (lam : picEt C (overSpec k B))
      = PicEtAff.unit C B (relPicMk C (overSpec k B) D.cechPicClass))
    (p : PrimeSpectrum B) :
    (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = 1 := by
  haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
    instIsIntegralBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
  haveI : QuasiCompact
      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
    instQuasiCompactBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField

/-- The comparison of sections on a datum piece with sections on its base change. -/
noncomputable def piecesMap : ∀ j : D.index,
    Γ(relCurve C B, D.pieces j) →+*
      Γ(relCurve C B', (D.baseChange B').pieces j)
  | .inl j => pieceSectionsMap B' (fiberChart₀ pi) (D.h₀ j)
  | .inr j => pieceSectionsMap B' (fiberChart₁ pi) (D.h₁ j)

/-- Base change commutes with the basic-open localization defining each datum piece. -/
noncomputable def pieceTermBaseChange : ∀ j : D.index,
    B' ⊗[B] Γ(relCurve C B, D.pieces j) ≃ₐ[B']
      Γ(relCurve C B', (D.baseChange B').pieces j)
  | .inl j =>
      pieceTermBaseChangeAlg B' (fiberChart₀ pi)
        (fiberTwoCover pi).isAffineOpen₀.isCompact
        (fiberTwoCover pi).isAffineOpen₀.isQuasiSeparated
        (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C B (fiberTwoCover pi))
        (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C B' (fiberTwoCover pi)) (D.h₀ j)
  | .inr j =>
      pieceTermBaseChangeAlg B' (fiberChart₁ pi)
        (fiberTwoCover pi).isAffineOpen₁.isCompact
        (fiberTwoCover pi).isAffineOpen₁.isQuasiSeparated
        (relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C B (fiberTwoCover pi))
        (relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C B' (fiberTwoCover pi)) (D.h₁ j)

/-- The datum-piece base-change equivalence sends `1 ⊗ t` to the compared section. -/
theorem pieceTermBaseChange_one_tmul (j : D.index)
    (t : Γ(relCurve C B, D.pieces j)) :
    D.pieceTermBaseChange B' j ((1 : B') ⊗ₜ[B] t) = D.piecesMap B' j t := by
  cases j with
  | inl j =>
      exact pieceTermBaseChangeAlg_one_tmul B' (fiberChart₀ pi)
        (fiberTwoCover pi).isAffineOpen₀.isCompact
        (fiberTwoCover pi).isAffineOpen₀.isQuasiSeparated
        (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C B (fiberTwoCover pi))
        (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C B' (fiberTwoCover pi)) (D.h₀ j) t
  | inr j =>
      exact pieceTermBaseChangeAlg_one_tmul B' (fiberChart₁ pi)
        (fiberTwoCover pi).isAffineOpen₁.isCompact
        (fiberTwoCover pi).isAffineOpen₁.isQuasiSeparated
        (relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C B (fiberTwoCover pi))
        (relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C B' (fiberTwoCover pi)) (D.h₁ j) t

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]

/-- Compare a global glued section along a change of coefficient ring. -/
noncomputable def sectionsMapTop (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
    (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤)) :
    ↥(gluedSubmodule B' (D.baseChange B').pieces (D.baseChange B').unit ⊤) :=
  D.sectionsMap B' (by rw [Scheme.Hom.preimage_top]) s

/-- Components of the compared global section are the compared original components. -/
theorem component_sectionsMapTop (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
    (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤)) (j : D.index) :
    (D.baseChange B').component (D.sectionsMapTop B' s) j =
      D.toBasicOpenCoverData.piecesMap B' j (D.component s j) := by
  let htop : (⊤ : (relCurve C B').Opens) ≤
      relCurveMap C B B' ⁻¹ᵁ (⊤ : (relCurve C B).Opens) := by
    rw [Scheme.Hom.preimage_top]
  cases j with
  | inl j =>
      simpa only [sectionsMapTop, component, sectionsMap_coe,
        BasicOpenCocycleDatum.baseChange, BasicOpenCoverData.piecesMap,
        BasicOpenCoverData.pieces, BasicOpenCoverData.baseChange,
        Sum.elim_inl, pieceSectionsMap] using
        (relCurveMap C B B').appLE_resHom
          (le_inf le_top le_rfl : D.pieces (Sum.inl j) ≤ ⊤ ⊓ D.pieces (Sum.inl j))
          (D.sectionsMap_component_le B' htop (Sum.inl j))
          (D.toBasicOpenCoverData.baseChange_pieces_le_preimage B' (Sum.inl j))
          (le_inf le_top le_rfl : (D.baseChange B').pieces (Sum.inl j) ≤
            ⊤ ⊓ (D.baseChange B').pieces (Sum.inl j)) (s.val (Sum.inl j))
  | inr j =>
      simpa only [sectionsMapTop, component, sectionsMap_coe,
        BasicOpenCocycleDatum.baseChange, BasicOpenCoverData.piecesMap,
        BasicOpenCoverData.pieces, BasicOpenCoverData.baseChange,
        Sum.elim_inr, pieceSectionsMap] using
        (relCurveMap C B B').appLE_resHom
          (le_inf le_top le_rfl : D.pieces (Sum.inr j) ≤ ⊤ ⊓ D.pieces (Sum.inr j))
          (D.sectionsMap_component_le B' htop (Sum.inr j))
          (D.toBasicOpenCoverData.baseChange_pieces_le_preimage B' (Sum.inr j))
          (le_inf le_top le_rfl : (D.baseChange B').pieces (Sum.inr j) ≤
            ⊤ ⊓ (D.baseChange B').pieces (Sum.inr j)) (s.val (Sum.inr j))

variable {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]

set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 800000 in
-- The glued trivialization carries a large dependent family of section rings.
-- A nonzero global section of a cocycle-glued line bundle on an integral scheme is
-- nonzero in every nonempty trivializing piece.
theorem component_ne_zero_of_global_ne_zero
    [IsIntegral (relCurve C K)] (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C K pi)
    (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule K D.pieces D.unit ⊤)) (hs : s ≠ 0)
    (j : D.index) (hj : D.pieces j ≠ ⊥) : D.component s j ≠ 0 := by
  intro hcomponent
  apply hs
  have hUj : ((D.pieces j : Set (relCurve C K))).Nonempty := by
    rcases Set.eq_empty_or_nonempty (D.pieces j : Set (relCurve C K)) with h | h
    · exact (hj (by ext x; rw [h]; simp)).elim
    · exact h
  have hres : gluedRes K D.pieces D.unit (le_top : D.pieces j ≤ ⊤) s = 0 := by
    apply (gluedTriv K D.isGluingCocycle j le_rfl).injective
    rw [map_zero, gluedTriv_apply, gluedRes_coe]
    simpa only [component, Scheme.resHom_resHom] using hcomponent
  apply Subtype.ext
  funext i
  by_cases hi : D.pieces i = ⊥
  · have hopen : ⊤ ⊓ D.pieces i = ⊥ := by rw [hi]; simp
    letI : Subsingleton Γ(relCurve C K, ⊤ ⊓ D.pieces i) := hopen ▸ inferInstance
    exact Subsingleton.elim _ _
  · have hUi : ((D.pieces i : Set (relCurve C K))).Nonempty := by
      rcases Set.eq_empty_or_nonempty (D.pieces i : Set (relCurve C K)) with h | h
      · exact (hi (by ext x; rw [h]; simp)).elim
      · exact h
    have hUji : (((D.pieces j ⊓ D.pieces i : (relCurve C K).Opens) :
        Set (relCurve C K))).Nonempty := by
      simpa only [Opens.coe_inf] using
        nonempty_preirreducible_inter (D.pieces j).isOpen (D.pieces i).isOpen hUj hUi
    letI : Nonempty ↥((D.pieces j ⊓ D.pieces i : (relCurve C K).Opens) :
        Set (relCurve C K)) := by
      obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := hUji
      exact ⟨⟨x, hx⟩⟩
    have hinj : Function.Injective ((relCurve C K).resHom
        (show D.pieces j ⊓ D.pieces i ≤ ⊤ ⊓ D.pieces i by simp)) :=
      map_injective_of_isIntegral (H := this) (relCurve C K)
        (homOfLE (show D.pieces j ⊓ D.pieces i ≤ ⊤ ⊓ D.pieces i by simp))

  letI : Module.Finite P.cover.Carrier Q := P.h0_finite

    rw [← Module.rankAtStalk_eq]

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartCoverageNoDrop
import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.CoverageDrop
import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.ThetaDegree

/-!
# The translated rank-one cover brick

This file records the part of the separably-closed cover argument that is already consumable by
the landed fibre API.  A `BaseFieldTranslationDrop` keeps the input class `lambda` in the
presentation equation, chooses its base-field translating class explicitly, and records the
positive-twist/point-subtraction output.  The consumer below turns that output into the exact
`IsSplitWitness` shape used by `chartLocus`.

The arbitrary-affine family of `PicRankOneLocalPresentation` objects required by
`PicRankOneOpen` is deliberately not inferred from `h0 = 1` and `H1 = 0`: no such producer is
landed in the current API.  The final theorem therefore exposes the field-level consumer and
keeps that family producer as an explicit integration obligation.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
open TopologicalSpace Opposite

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

open AlgebraicJacobian

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

noncomputable section

/-! ## The positive-twist input -/

section PositiveTwist

variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral Y]
  [Y.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 1)]

/-- The FLV class theorem in the spelling used by the translated-cover lane.

The class `l` is the presenting class of the input fibre, while `theta` is the positive
base-field twist.  Keeping this as a named wrapper makes the positive-twist step visible at the
call site; it does not manufacture a presentation or hide the input class in an unrelated
existential. -/
theorem exists_positive_twist_vanishing
    (π : Y ⟶ P1 K) [IsFinite π] [IsDominant π]
    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap K = Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
    (l θ : Y.CechPic) (hθ : 1 ≤ classDeg K θ) :
    ∃ n₀ : ℕ, ∀ n ≥ n₀, ∀ W : Y.CurveDivisor,
      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K W = l * θ ^ n →
        Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K W) 1) := by
  exact exists_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_one_le_classDeg_of_isFinite_toP1
    π hπ l θ hθ

end PositiveTwist

/-! ## The lambda-tied drop package -/

section DropPackage

variable {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
  [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra K L] [IsScalarTower k K L]
  [Module.Finite K L] [Algebra.IsSeparable K L]

/-- Data for the positive twist and the subsequent point subtraction.

`hM₀` ties the splitting field presentation to the particular input `mu`; `hW₀` says that the
divisor being reduced is in the positive twist class (the chart index is zero at this stage).
`baseSubtraction` is intentionally an explicit class-level bridge: it says that the divisor
returned by the greedy reduction is represented by a base-field divisor.  The current tree has
the graph-class version of this bridge but no divisor pullback operation, so this hypothesis is
kept visible rather than replaced by a fieldwise existential. -/
structure SepClosedTranslatedDropData (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K)) where
  m : ℕ
  M₀ : (relCurve C L).CechPic
  hM₀ : PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K μ) =
    PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M₀)
  W₀ : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor
  hW₀ : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W₀ =
    M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
      (chartTwistClass C m (0 : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor))
  genusValue : ℕ
  excess : ℕ
  hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (genusValue : ℤ)
  hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W₀ = (genusValue : ℤ) + excess
  h1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
    ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W₀) 1)
  P : Set ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)
  hdense : ∀ U : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).Opens,
    (U : Set ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)).Nonempty → (P ∩ U).Nonempty
  hPcl : ∀ x ∈ P, x ≠ genericPoint ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)
  hPdeg : ∀ x ∈ P, ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).residueDeg L x = 1
  baseSubtraction : ∀ (S : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor),
    0 ≤ S → Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L S = (excess : ℤ) →
      (∀ (x : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint _),
        coeffAt hx S ≠ 0 → x ∈ P) →
      ∃ Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor,
        Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L S =
          Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
            ((chartTwistClass C 0 Z)⁻¹)

/-- The output of the positive-twist/drop construction, tied to both the input class and the
base-field translating divisor.

The final field is the existing fibre consumer.  In particular, `S` is not merely a divisor
with the right cohomology: `baseClass` identifies its class with the base change of `Z`, and
`translated` is about `mu` translated by the resulting base-field class
`chartTwistClass C d.m Z`. -/
structure SepClosedTranslatedDropResult (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K))
    (d : SepClosedTranslatedDropData (C := C) (L := L) μ) where
  S : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor
  Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor
  nonnegative : 0 ≤ S
  degree : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L S = (d.excess : ℤ)
  support : ∀ (x : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint _),
    coeffAt hx S ≠ 0 → x ∈ d.P
  baseClass : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L S =
    Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) ((chartTwistClass C 0 Z)⁻¹)
  h0_one : Sheaf.h0
    ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L (d.W₀ - S)) = 1
  h1_vanishing : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
    ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L (d.W₀ - S)) 1)
  translated : IsSplitWitness C
    (μ * thetaFamily C (chartTwistClass C d.m Z) (overSpec k K))

/-- Positive twisting followed by point subtraction produces the exact field-level translated
rank-one witness.

The greedy theorem supplies `S`, `h0 = 1`, and preservation of `H1 = 0`.  The explicit
`baseSubtraction` bridge then supplies the base divisor `Z`; class arithmetic shows that
`W₀ - S` presents `mu` translated by the base-field class `chartTwistClass C d.m Z`.  The last
line applies the existing `IsSplitWitness` consumer, so no unrelated Picard class can satisfy
the conclusion. -/
theorem exists_sepClosedTranslatedDropResult
    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K))
    (d : SepClosedTranslatedDropData (C := C) (L := L) μ) :
    Nonempty (SepClosedTranslatedDropResult (C := C) (L := L) μ d) := by
  obtain ⟨-, S, hS0, hSdeg, hSsupport, hS0one, hS1⟩ :=
    exists_isSplitWitness_of_drop C μ d.m
      (0 : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
      d.genusValue d.excess d.hχ d.M₀ d.hM₀ d.W₀ d.hW₀ d.hdeg d.h1
      d.P d.hdense d.hPcl d.hPdeg
  obtain ⟨Z, hSZ⟩ := d.baseSubtraction S hS0 hSdeg hSsupport
  have hW : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L (d.W₀ - S) =
      d.M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
        (chartTwistClass C d.m Z) := by
    have hW₀ := d.hW₀
    unfold relCurveMap relCurve at hW₀ hSZ ⊢
    rw [sub_eq_add_neg, Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_add, Scheme.picClass_neg,
      hW₀, hSZ]
    simp only [map_inv, inv_inv]
    rw [mul_assoc, ← map_mul]
    simp only [chartTwistClass, Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_zero, inv_one, mul_one,
      pow_zero, one_mul]
  have htranslated : IsSplitWitness C
      (μ * thetaFamily C (chartTwistClass C d.m Z) (overSpec k K)) :=
    isSplitWitness_of_witness_twistClass C μ d.m Z d.M₀ d.hM₀
      (d.W₀ - S) hW hS1
  exact ⟨{
    S := S
    Z := Z
    nonnegative := hS0
    degree := hSdeg
    support := hSsupport
    baseClass := hSZ
    h0_one := hS0one
    h1_vanishing := hS1
    translated := htranslated
  }⟩

end DropPackage

end

end AlgebraicGeometry

/-!
# Rational-point residue bridge for the translated cover

The density oracle used by the translated-cover drop has to record residue degree one at the
chosen points.  This file supplies that arithmetic bridge from the actual section certificate,
rather than adding `residueDeg = 1` as an unrelated existential field.  The relative specialization
is the exact point produced by `Over.rationalPointBaseChange`.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
open TopologicalSpace Opposite

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

open AlgebraicJacobian

attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver

/-! ## Sections have residue degree one -/

theorem residueDeg_one_of_section
    {K : Type u} [Field K]
    {X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))}
    {e : Spec (CommRingCat.of K) ⟶ X.left}
    (he : e ≫ X.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)))
    {x : X.left}
    (hx : e.base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K) = x) :
    X.left.residueDeg K x = 1 := by
  letI : Algebra K (X.left.presheaf.stalk x) := stalkAlgebra X.hom x
  have h := bijective_algebraMap_residueField_of_section X he hx
  have hmap :
      algebraMap K (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (X.left.presheaf.stalk x)) =
        X.left.residueOverAlgebraMap K x := by
    ext c
    rw [IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply K (X.left.presheaf.stalk x)
      (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (X.left.presheaf.stalk x)),
      IsLocalRing.ResidueField.algebraMap_eq, Scheme.residueOverAlgebraMap,
      algebraMap_overStalkAlgebra]
    simp [stalkStructureHom, Scheme.overAlgebraMap]
    rfl
  letI : Algebra K (X.left.residueField x) :=
    (X.left.residueOverAlgebraMap K x).toAlgebra
  unfold Scheme.residueDeg
  change Module.finrank K (X.left.residueField x) = 1
  apply Module.finrank_of_bijective_algebraMap
  change Function.Bijective (X.left.residueOverAlgebraMap K x)
  rw [← hmap]
  exact h

/-! ## The base-changed rational point is such a section -/

theorem residueDeg_one_of_rationalPointBaseChange
    {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    (p : Spec (.of k) ⟶ C.left)
    (hp : p ≫ C.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k))) :
    ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).residueDeg L
      ((Over.rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp).base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint L)) = 1 := by
  apply residueDeg_one_of_section
    (X := Over.mk (snd C (overSpec k L)).left)
    (e := Over.rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp)
  · exact Over.rationalPointBaseChange_snd C L p hp
  · rfl

/-- The graph point of a field-valued point has residue degree one. -/
theorem residueDeg_one_of_graphPoint
    {k K : Type u} [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    (t : overSpec k K ⟶ C) :
    (C ⊗ overSpec k K).left.residueDeg K (Over.graphPoint C t) = 1 := by
  exact residueDeg_one_of_section
    (X := Over.mk (snd C (overSpec k K)).left)
    (e := (Over.sectionOfPoint t).left)
    (by
      exact congrArg (fun q : overSpec k K ⟶ overSpec k K => q.left)
        (Over.sectionOfPoint_snd t))
    (by
      change (Over.sectionOfPoint t).left.base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K) =
        (Over.sectionOfPoint t).left.base default
      exact congrArg (Over.sectionOfPoint t).left.base
        (Subsingleton.elim _ _))

/-- The graph presentation has multiplicity one at its graph point.

`presentationDivisor_graphLocalEquations` initially records the multiplicity as an order.
The graph class and its residue field both have degree one, so the degree formula forces that
order to be one.  This is the pointwise input for finite-support class descent below. -/
theorem graphPicClass_eq_picClass_single
    {k K : Type u} [Field k] [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    (t : overSpec k K ⟶ C) :
    Over.graphPicClass C t =
      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K
        (Scheme.CurveDivisor.single (graphPoint_ne_genericPoint C t) 1) := by
  let hx := graphPoint_ne_genericPoint C t
  let a : ℤ :=
    Multiplicative.toAdd
      (Scheme.ordZ ((C ⊗ overSpec k K).left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
        hx ((Over.graphLocalEquations C t).presentation.elem (Over.graphPoint C t)))
  have hsingle :
      Scheme.presentationDivisor K (Over.graphLocalEquations C t).presentation =
        Scheme.CurveDivisor.single hx a := by
    exact presentationDivisor_graphLocalEquations C t
  have hclass :
      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K (Scheme.CurveDivisor.single hx a) =
        Over.graphPicClass C t := by
    rw [← hsingle, Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_presentationDivisor K,
      Scheme.LocalEquations.presentation_picClass]
    rfl
  have hdeg := classDeg_graphPicClass C t
  rw [← hclass, classDeg_picClass, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_single'] at hdeg
  rw [residueDeg_one_of_graphPoint C t, Nat.cast_one, mul_one] at hdeg
  rw [hdeg] at hclass
  exact hclass.symm

/-! ## Image-set packaging -/

theorem residueDeg_one_of_mem_rationalPointBaseChange_image
    {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    (P : Set (relCurve C L))
    (hP : ∀ x ∈ P, ∃ (p : Spec (.of k) ⟶ C.left)
      (hp : p ≫ C.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k))),
      (Over.rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp).base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint L) = x) :
    ∀ x ∈ P, (relCurve C L).residueDeg L x = 1 := by
  intro x hx
  obtain ⟨p, hp, hpx⟩ := hP x hx
  rw [← hpx]
  exact residueDeg_one_of_rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp

/-! ## The dense point image used by the drop oracle -/

/-- The points obtained by base-changing actual `k`-rational sections of `C` to `L`.

The section certificate is retained in the membership predicate, so later consumers can recover
the base point and its exact residue-degree proof.  This is deliberately an image set, rather
than an existential carrier unrelated to the chosen curve and extension. -/
def rationalPointBaseChangeImage
    {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] : Set (relCurve C L) :=
  {x | ∃ (p : Spec (.of k) ⟶ C.left)
      (hp : p ≫ C.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k))),
      (Over.rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp).base
        (IsLocalRing.closedPoint L) = x}

/-- Base-changed `k`-rational points are dense over a separably closed base. -/
theorem dense_rationalPointBaseChangeImage
    {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsSepClosed k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsIntegral C.left]
    (U : (relCurve C L).Opens)
    (hU : (U : Set (relCurve C L)).Nonempty) :
    (rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L ∩ U).Nonempty := by
  obtain ⟨p, hp, hmem⟩ := Over.dense_baseChange_rationalPoints C L U hU
  exact ⟨_, ⟨⟨p, hp, rfl⟩, hmem⟩⟩

/-- Every point in the dense image has residue degree one, by its retained section certificate. -/
theorem residueDeg_one_of_mem_rationalPointBaseChangeImage'
    {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
    ∀ x ∈ rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L,
      (relCurve C L).residueDeg L x = 1 := by
  intro x hx
  obtain ⟨p, hp, hpx⟩ := hx
  rw [← hpx]
  exact residueDeg_one_of_rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp

/-! ## Class descent for divisors supported on the rational-point image -/

/-- Every point in the rational-point image is non-generic.  The retained section certificate
identifies it with an actual graph point, where `graphPoint_ne_genericPoint` applies. -/
theorem ne_genericPoint_of_mem_rationalPointBaseChangeImage
    {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
    ∀ x ∈ rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L,
      x ≠ genericPoint (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left := by
  intro x hx
  obtain ⟨p, hp, hpx⟩ := hx
  rw [← hpx]
  let q : overSpec k k ⟶ C := Over.homMk p (by
    rw [overSpec_self_hom]
    exact hp)
  change Over.graphPoint C
      (Over.overSpecMap (Algebra.ofId k L) ≫ q) ≠
        genericPoint (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left
  exact graphPoint_ne_genericPoint C _

/-- The one-point divisor at a base-changed rational point is the base change of a class on the
base curve.  This is deliberately a class statement: no pullback operation on Weil divisors is
needed. -/
theorem exists_baseClass_picClass_single_of_mem_rationalPointBaseChangeImage
    {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    (x : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)
    (hx : x ≠ genericPoint (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)
    (hmem : x ∈ rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L) :
    ∃ c : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CechPic,
      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L (Scheme.CurveDivisor.single hx 1) =
        Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) c := by
  obtain ⟨p, hp, hpx⟩ := hmem
  let q : overSpec k k ⟶ C := Over.homMk p (by
    rw [overSpec_self_hom]
    exact hp)
  change Over.graphPoint C
      (Over.overSpecMap (Algebra.ofId k L) ≫ q) = x at hpx
  subst x
  refine ⟨Over.graphPicClass C q, ?_⟩
  rw [← graphPicClass_eq_picClass_single C]
  exact graphPicClass_base_of_field C L q

/-- Exact discharge of `SepClosedTranslatedDropData.baseSubtraction` for the rational-point
image.  The descended class is re-presented by an actual base-field divisor `Z`; at exponent
zero, the inverse of `chartTwistClass C 0 Z` is precisely `picClass k Z`. -/
theorem exists_baseSubtraction_of_supported_on_rationalPointBaseChangeImage
    {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    (S : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.CurveDivisor)
    (hsupp : ∀ (x : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)
      (hx : x ≠ genericPoint (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left),
      coeffAt hx S ≠ 0 → x ∈ rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L) :
    ∃ Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor,
      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L S =
        Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
          ((chartTwistClass C 0 Z)⁻¹) := by
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ :=
    exists_baseClass_of_supported_on_rationalPointBaseChangeImage C S hsupp
  obtain ⟨Z, hZ⟩ := Scheme.CurveDivisor.exists_picClass_eq k c
  refine ⟨Z, ?_⟩
  rw [hc]
  apply congrArg
  simp only [chartTwistClass, pow_zero, one_mul]
  rw [hZ]
  exact (inv_inv c).symm

    (hW₀ : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W₀ =
      M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
        (chartTwistClass C m (0 : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)))
    (excess : ℕ)
    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W₀ = (genus C : ℤ) + excess)
    (h1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
      ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W₀) 1)) :
    SepClosedTranslatedDropData (C := C) (L := L) μ where
  m := m
  M₀ := M₀
  hM₀ := hM₀
  W₀ := W₀
  hW₀ := hW₀
  genusValue := genus C
  excess := excess
  hχ := chi_moduleKSheaf C

  hPcl := ne_genericPoint_of_mem_rationalPointBaseChangeImage C

    intro S _ _ hsupp

        μ m M₀ hM₀ W₀ hW₀ excess hdeg h1)) := by
  exact exists_sepClosedTranslatedDropResult μ

    10	# DAT-B B-1 — the oracle-parametrized greedy `h⁰`-drop to `h⁰ = 1`
    11	
    12	The coverage-side normalization of the DAT-B worksheet (`informal/w4-datb-worksheet.md`
    13	§1.4, COV-2): on the curve bundle `Y` over a field `K` (the fibre field of the coverage
    14	argument), given an **admissible point oracle** `P` — a set of closed `K`-rational points
    15	(`residueDeg = 1`) meeting every nonempty open — and a divisor `W` of degree `g + e` with
    16	`H¹(𝒪(W)) = 0`, there is an effective divisor `Σ` of degree `e` supported in `P` with
    17	
    18	  `h⁰(𝒪(W − Σ)) = 1`  and  `H¹(𝒪(W − Σ)) = 0`
    19	  (`exists_effective_sub_h0_eq_one`, the keystone).
    20	
    21	The pointwise coverage theorem (B-5, worksheet §1.2 step 5) consumes this with
    22	`P :=` the base-changed `C(K_s)`-points supplied by the density oracle of B-2
    23	(`Curve/SepPointsDense.lean`); the oracle parametrization decouples the density
    24	discharge from the pure Riemann–Roch drop.
    25	
    26	## Route (worksheet §1.4, per step for the current `W'` with `h¹ = 0`, `deg = g + e'`)
    27	
    28	* **The bad locus is small** (`exists_admissible_nonbase_point`): `H⁰(𝒪(W'))` is nonzero
    29	  (rank anchor `h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one`), its base divisor
    30	  (`Scheme.baseDivisor`, the DD-F kit) has finite support consisting of closed points, so
    31	  the non-base locus contains a nonempty open (complement of a finite closed set in the
    32	  irreducible curve — it contains the generic point) and the oracle supplies an admissible
    33	  point there; the base-divisor achiever (`exists_coeffAt_eq_baseDivisorAt`) turns
    34	  "outside the support" into an exact-order section.
    35	* **Exact drop at a rational non-base point** (`h0_sub_single_of_rational_nonbase`):
    36	  `h⁰(𝒪(W' − x)) ≤ h⁰(𝒪(W')) − 1` — sections of `W' − x` are sections of `W'`, a *proper*
    37	  submodule since the non-base section violates the deeper pole bound at `x`
    38	  (`Submodule.finrank_lt_finrank_of_lt` through the `h⁰` bridge
    39	  `finrank_divisorSections_top`) — while the χ-ledger (`chi_divisorSheaf`) with
    40	  `residueDeg x = 1` and `h¹(𝒪(W')) = 0` gives `χ(𝒪(W' − x)) = h⁰(𝒪(W')) − 1`; equality
    41	  forces BOTH `h⁰(𝒪(W' − x)) = h⁰(𝒪(W')) − 1` AND `h¹(𝒪(W' − x)) = 0` — the induction
    42	  invariant.
    43	* **Terminate at `e' = 0`**: `h⁰ = 1` by the rank anchor at `deg = g`, `χ(𝒪) = 1 − g`.

   154	    refine CurveDivisor.le_iff_coeffAt.mpr (fun y hy => ?_)

   200	/-- **COV-2, the oracle-parametrized greedy `h⁰`-drop** (★ B-1 keystone, worksheet §1.4):

   210	drop (`h0_sub_single_of_rational_nonbase`) preserves the invariant `h¹ = 0` while

   212	`P` with the base-changed `C(K_s)`-points of B-2. -/
   213	theorem exists_effective_sub_h0_eq_one (g : ℕ)
   214	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (Y.moduleKSheaf K) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
   215	    (P : Set Y)
   216	    (hdense : ∀ U : Y.Opens, (U : Set Y).Nonempty → (P ∩ U).Nonempty)
   217	    (hPcl : ∀ x ∈ P, x ≠ genericPoint Y)
   218	    (hPdeg : ∀ x ∈ P, Y.residueDeg K x = 1)
   219	    (W : Y.CurveDivisor) (e : ℕ)
   220	    (hdeg : CurveDivisor.deg K W = (g : ℤ) + e)
   221	    (h1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K W) 1)) :
   222	    ∃ S : Y.CurveDivisor, 0 ≤ S ∧ CurveDivisor.deg K S = (e : ℤ) ∧
   223	      (∀ (x : Y) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y), coeffAt hx S ≠ 0 → x ∈ P) ∧
   224	      Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - S)) = 1 ∧
   225	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - S)) 1) := by
   226	  suffices H : ∀ (e : ℕ) (W : Y.CurveDivisor),
   227	      CurveDivisor.deg K W = (g : ℤ) + e →
   228	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K W) 1) →
   229	      ∃ S : Y.CurveDivisor, 0 ≤ S ∧ CurveDivisor.deg K S = (e : ℤ) ∧
   230	        (∀ (x : Y) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y), coeffAt hx S ≠ 0 → x ∈ P) ∧
   231	        Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - S)) = 1 ∧
   232	        Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - S)) 1) from
   233	    H e W hdeg h1
   234	  intro e
   235	  induction e with
   236	  | zero =>
   237	    intro W hdeg h1
   238	    have hanchor := h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one (K := K) W h1
   239	    rw [hχ, hdeg] at hanchor
   240	    refine ⟨0, le_refl 0, by rw [CurveDivisor.deg_zero, Nat.cast_zero], ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
   241	    · intro x hx hne
   242	      exact (hne (CurveDivisor.coeffAt_zero hx)).elim
   243	    · rw [sub_zero]
   244	      push_cast at hanchor
   245	      omega
   246	    · rw [sub_zero]
   247	      exact h1
   248	  | succ e ih =>
   249	    intro W hdeg h1
   250	    -- `h⁰(𝒪(W)) = e + 2 > 0` by the rank anchor
   251	    have hanchor := h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one (K := K) W h1
   252	    rw [hχ, hdeg] at hanchor

   254	      push_cast at hanchor
   255	      omega
   256	    -- an admissible non-base point and the exact drop there
   257	    obtain ⟨x, hx, hxP, f, hfW, hf, hnb⟩ :=
   258	      exists_admissible_nonbase_point P hdense hPcl W hpos

   260	      h0_sub_single_of_rational_nonbase W h1 hx (hPdeg x hxP) hfW hf hnb
   261	    have hdeg' : CurveDivisor.deg K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1) = (g : ℤ) + e := by
   262	      rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_sub' K, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_single' K hx 1,
   263	        hPdeg x hxP, Nat.cast_one, mul_one, hdeg]
   264	      push_cast
   265	      ring
   266	    obtain ⟨S', hS'0, hS'deg, hS'P, hS'h0, hS'h1⟩ :=
   267	      ih (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1) hdeg' h1'
   268	    have hsplit : W - (S' + CurveDivisor.single hx 1)
   269	        = W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1 - S' := by
   270	      abel
   271	    refine ⟨S' + CurveDivisor.single hx 1, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
   272	    · -- effectivity
   273	      refine CurveDivisor.le_iff_coeffAt.mpr (fun y hy => ?_)
   274	      have h0S' := CurveDivisor.le_iff_coeffAt.mp hS'0 y hy
   275	      rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_zero] at h0S'
   276	      rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_zero, CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add]
   277	      by_cases hyx : y = x
   278	      · subst hyx
   279	        rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_single_self]
   280	        omega
   281	      · rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_single_of_ne hx hy hyx]
   282	        omega
   283	    · -- degree
   284	      rw [CurveDivisor.deg_add, hS'deg, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_single' K hx 1,
   285	        hPdeg x hxP, Nat.cast_one, mul_one]
   286	      push_cast
   287	      ring
   288	    · -- support in `P`
   289	      intro y hy hne
   290	      rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add] at hne
   291	      by_cases hyx : y = x
   292	      · subst hyx
   293	        exact hxP
   294	      · rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_single_of_ne hx hy hyx, add_zero] at hne
   295	        exact hS'P y hy hne
   296	    · rw [hsplit]
   297	      exact hS'h0
   298	    · rw [hsplit]
   299	      exact hS'h1

    18	
    19	An element of `picDegLayerFunctor` is an etale-plus class, not a chosen line bundle.  The
    20	rank-one route therefore needs an explicit local presentation before it can use the evaluation
    21	map of a line bundle.  `PicRankOneLocalPresentation` records that presentation on an affine
    22	test and ties every piece of data to the input class:
    23	
    24	* a descent-class representative whose plus class is the affine collapse of the input;
    25	* a cocycle datum presenting that same relative Picard class;
    26	* a locally free rank-one `Scheme.Modules` object whose base-ring sheaf is the datum's sheaf;
    27	* invertibility of the canonical native pushforward base-change mate on every cartesian square;
    28	* the cohomological rank-one outputs used by the evaluation construction.
    29	
    30	No existence, openness, or representability assertion is made here.  The first canonical
    31	consumer is `PicRankOneLocalPresentation.evaluation`, the pullback-pushforward counit.
    32	The method `PicRankOneLocalPresentation.h0BaseChange` derives arbitrary affine base change
    33	from the same presentation's `H^1`-vanishing field.  The section bridge at the end identifies
    34	datum `H^0` with native global sections and proves, by the adjunction triangle identity, that
    35	the evaluation counit sends the canonical unit-lift back to that same section.

    10	# Restricting a scheme module to the base ring
    11	
    12	For a scheme `X` over `Spec k`, this file views an `X.Modules` object as a sheaf of
    13	`k`-modules.  The construction keeps the same section types and restriction maps; only the
    14	scalar action is restricted along `k -> Gamma(X, U)`.  It is the dialect bridge needed to
    15	compare a `Scheme.Modules` line bundle with the fixed-base module sheaves used by the Cech
    16	cohomology engine.
    17	-/

    41	  r • x

    43	/-- The presheaf underlying a scheme module after restriction of scalars to the base ring. -/
    44	noncomputable def toModuleKPresheafOfModules
    45	    (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) (M : X.left.Modules) :
    46	    X.left.Opensᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} k where
    47	  obj U := ModuleCat.of k Γ(M, U.unop)
    48	  map {U V} f := ModuleCat.ofHom
    49	    { toFun := fun x => M.presheaf.map f x
    50	      map_add' := fun x y => map_add _ x y
    51	      map_smul' := fun r x =>
    52	        (Scheme.Modules.map_smul M f.unop (X.left.overAlgebraMap k U.unop r) x).trans
    53	          (congrArg
    54	            (fun (s : Γ(X.left, V.unop)) =>
    55	              smulSection X M V.unop s (M.presheaf.map f x))
    56	            (X.left.overAlgebraMap_apply_res k f r)) }
    57	  map_id U := by
    58	    ext x
    59	    exact congrFun (congrArg (fun (f : M.presheaf.obj U ⟶ M.presheaf.obj U) =>
    60	      (ConcreteCategory.hom f : _ → _)) (M.presheaf.map_id U)) x
    61	  map_comp {U V W} f g := by
    62	    ext x
    63	    exact congrFun (congrArg (fun (h : M.presheaf.obj U ⟶ M.presheaf.obj W) =>
    64	      (ConcreteCategory.hom h : _ → _)) (M.presheaf.map_comp f g)) x

    67	lemma toModuleKPresheafOfModules_isSheaf

    69	    Presheaf.IsSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.left.toTopCat)

    78	    Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.left.toTopCat) (ModuleCat.{u} k) :=

    12	/-!
    13	# Invertible sections of a cocycle-glued line bundle on an affine open
    14	
    15	The cocycle pieces used to construct `gluedSheaf` need not contain an arbitrary affine
    16	open.  Nevertheless, every affine open admits a finite basic-open refinement subordinate
    17	to the canonical pointed cover by those pieces.  On each refined basic open the glued
    18	sheaf is free of rank one.  The existing localization-span engine then proves that its
    19	sections on the original affine open are finite projective.
    20	
    21	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.AffineSectionsModel` packages the quasi-coherent action chosen by
    22	that internal refinement together with the finite, projective, and invertible instances.
    23	Returning a `Nonempty` model keeps the refinement choice noncomputable while giving
    24	downstream code a single datum from which it can install all four compatible instances.
    25	
    26	This is the chart-free line-bundle substrate needed to restrict a positive theta twist to
    27	the arbitrary affine pieces of `AffAdaptation`: the divisor cover is not required to lie in
    28	either pinned theta chart.
    29	-/
    30	
    31	set_option autoImplicit false
    32	
    33	universe u
    34	
    35	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite TopologicalSpace
    36	open scoped TensorProduct
    37

    41	
    42	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    43	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
    44	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom pi]
    45	
    46	namespace BasicOpenCocycleDatum
    47	
    48	/-- A compatible quasi-coherent module structure on the sections of a cocycle-glued
    49	line bundle over an affine open, together with its finite projective rank-one properties.
    50	
    51	The module instance is written explicitly in the fields so that it is definitionally the
    52	one induced by `qcoh`; a consumer may install `M.qcoh` and recover `M.finite` and
    53	`M.projective` without any proof-irrelevance transport. -/
    54	structure AffineSectionsModel (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
    55	    (V : (relCurve C B).Opens) where
    56	  qcoh : Scheme.QcohOn D.sheaf V
    57	  qsmul_eq : ∀ {W : (relCurve C B).Opens} (hWV : W ≤ V) (r : Γ(relCurve C B, V))
    58	      (s : D.sheaf.obj.obj (op W)),
    59	      letI := qcoh
    60	      Scheme.QcohOn.qsmul (F := D.sheaf) hWV r s =
    61	        gluedQsmul B D.pieces D.unit hWV r s
    62	  finite : @Module.Finite Γ(relCurve C B, V) (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op V))
    63	    _ _ (@Scheme.QcohOn.moduleOfLE B _ (relCurve C B) V D.sheaf qcoh V (le_refl V))
    64	  projective : @Module.Projective Γ(relCurve C B, V) _
    65	    (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op V)) _
    66	    (@Scheme.QcohOn.moduleOfLE B _ (relCurve C B) V D.sheaf qcoh V (le_refl V))
    67	  invertible : @Module.Invertible Γ(relCurve C B, V) (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op V))
    68	    _ _ (@Scheme.QcohOn.moduleOfLE B _ (relCurve C B) V D.sheaf qcoh V (le_refl V))
    69	
    70	/-- Sections of a cocycle-glued line bundle on every affine open admit a compatible
    71	invertible module model.  The proof chooses a finite basic-open refinement of the canonical
    72	pointed cover, trivializes after the resulting faithfully flat product localization, and
    73	descends invertibility; finiteness and projectivity are recorded on the same action. -/
    74	theorem nonempty_affineSectionsModel (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
    75	    (V : (relCurve C B).Opens) (hV : IsAffineOpen V) :
    76	    Nonempty (D.AffineSectionsModel V) := by
    77	  classical
    78	  obtain ⟨ι, fint, f, anchor, coeff, hP, hpart⟩ :=
    79	    hV.exists_finite_basicOpen_refinement D.pointedCover
    80	  letI : Fintype ι := fint
    81	  let sigma : ι → D.index := fun i => D.pieceIndex (anchor i)
    82	  have hP' : ∀ i : ι, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i) ≤ D.pieces (sigma i) := hP
    83	  have hcov : V ≤ ⨆ i : ι, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i) :=
    84	    le_iSup_basicOpen_of_sum_eq_one coeff f hpart
    85	  let q : Scheme.QcohOn D.sheaf V :=
    86	    gluedQcohOn B D.pieces D.unit D.isGluingCocycle hP' hcov
    87	  letI : Scheme.QcohOn D.sheaf V := q
    88	  let m : Module Γ(relCurve C B, V) (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op V)) :=
    89	    Scheme.QcohOn.moduleOfLE (F := D.sheaf) (le_refl V)
    90	  have hspan : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤ :=
    91	    Ideal.span_range_eq_top_of_sum_eq_one coeff f hpart
    92	  have hfin : @Module.Finite Γ(relCurve C B, V) (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op V)) _ _ m :=
    93	    moduleFinite_glued B D.pieces D.unit hV D.isGluingCocycle
    94	      (fun _ _ _ => rfl) hP' hspan
    95	  have hproj : @Module.Projective Γ(relCurve C B, V) _
    96	      (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op V)) _ m :=
    97	    projective_glued B D.pieces D.unit hV D.isGluingCocycle
    98	      (fun _ _ _ => rfl) hP' hspan
    99	  letI pieceBaseModule : ∀ i : ι, Module Γ(relCurve C B, V)
   100	      (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op ((relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i)))) := fun i =>
   101	    Scheme.QcohOn.moduleOfLE (F := D.sheaf) ((relCurve C B).basicOpen_le (f i))
   102	  letI pieceModule : ∀ i : ι,
   103	      Module Γ(relCurve C B, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i))
   104	        (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op ((relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i)))) := fun i =>
   105	    gluedPieceModule B D.pieces D.unit D.isGluingCocycle hP' i
   106	  letI pieceTower : ∀ i : ι, IsScalarTower Γ(relCurve C B, V)
   107	      Γ(relCurve C B, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i))
   108	      (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op ((relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i)))) := fun i =>
   109	    isScalarTower_chart_piece B D.pieces D.unit D.isGluingCocycle
   110	      (fun _ _ _ => rfl) hP' i
   111	  letI pieceLocalization : ∀ i : ι, IsLocalization.Away (f i)
   112	      Γ(relCurve C B, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i)) := fun i =>
   113	    hV.isLocalization_basicOpen (f i)
   114	  haveI pieceLocalized : ∀ i : ι, IsLocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers (f i))
   115	      (Scheme.QcohOn.secResₗ (F := D.sheaf)
   116	        ((relCurve C B).basicOpen_le (f i)) (le_refl V)) := fun i =>
   117	    isLocalizedModule_secResₗ_glued B D.pieces D.unit hV D.isGluingCocycle
   118	      (fun _ _ _ => rfl) hP' i
   119	  let e (i : ι) :
   120	      Γ(relCurve C B, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i)) ⊗[Γ(relCurve C B, V)]
   121	          (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op V))
   122	        ≃ₗ[Γ(relCurve C B, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i))]
   123	          Γ(relCurve C B, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i)) :=
   124	    (IsLocalizedModule.isBaseChange (Submonoid.powers (f i))
   125	      Γ(relCurve C B, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i))
   126	      (Scheme.QcohOn.secResₗ (F := D.sheaf)
   127	        ((relCurve C B).basicOpen_le (f i)) (le_refl V))).equiv.trans
   128	      (gluedPieceEquiv B D.pieces D.unit D.isGluingCocycle hP' i)
   129	  letI : Module.FaithfullyFlat Γ(relCurve C B, V)
   130	      (∀ i : ι, Γ(relCurve C B, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i))) :=
   131	    Module.FaithfullyFlat.pi_of_span_eq_top f hspan
   132	  let E := Module.piTrivialization e
   133	  letI : Module.Invertible
   134	      (∀ i : ι, Γ(relCurve C B, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i)))
   135	      ((∀ i : ι, Γ(relCurve C B, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i))) ⊗[Γ(relCurve C B, V)]
   136	        (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op V))) :=
   137	    Module.Invertible.congr E.symm
   138	  have hinv : @Module.Invertible Γ(relCurve C B, V) (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op V)) _ _ m :=
   139	    Module.Invertible.of_invertible_tensorProduct_of_faithfullyFlat
   140	      Γ(relCurve C B, V)
   141	      (∀ i : ι, Γ(relCurve C B, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (f i)))
   142	      (D.sheaf.obj.obj (op V))
   143	  exact ⟨{
   144	    qcoh := q
   145	    qsmul_eq := fun _ _ _ => rfl
   146	    finite := hfin
   147	    projective := hproj
   148	    invertible := hinv
   149	  }⟩

    18	  `∑ j, a_j · h_j = 1` per pinned chart; `pieces` sends `J₀ ⊕ J₁` to the basic opens
    19	  `D(h_j)`.
    20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum` — the cover data together with the
    21	  transition units on the pairwise basic-open overlaps (`Units` bundle the inverse
    22	  witnesses) and the cocycle law `Scheme.IsGluingCocycle`.
    23	* `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.sheaf` — the glued sheaf of `B`-modules of the datum
    24	  (`gluedSheaf`), with the quasi-coherence packagings on **both pinned charts** and on
    25	  the **overlap** as instances (`instQcohOn₀/₁/Inf`, from `gluedQcohOn`: side-`i`'s own
    26	  family on chart `i`; side-0's family restricted along `V₀ᴮ ⊓ V₁ᴮ ≤ V₀ᴮ` on the
    27	  overlap, through the subordinate-pieces interface).
    28	* `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.pairData` — the two-cover pair data at the pinned relative
    29	  coordinates `t₀ᴮ, t₁ᴮ` (`relFiberCoord₀/₁`), through `gluedPairData` (the
    30	  componentwise-action hypotheses are `rfl` for the keyed instances).
    31	
    32	The engine keystones fired on `pairData.pair` are in
    33	`AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.GluedSheafEngine`.
    34	-/

    43	namespace AlgebraicGeometry

    45	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule
    46	
    47	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    48	variable (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
    49	variable (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k)
    50	
    51	/-- **The basic-open cover data over `B`** (worksheet §3.2, first half): finite index
    52	types `J₀, J₁`, for `j ∈ Jᵢ` a section `h_j` of the pinned chart `Vᵢᴮ` with partition
    53	witnesses `∑ j, a_j · h_j = 1` in `Γ(Vᵢᴮ, 𝒪)` — so the basic opens `D(h_j)` cover the
    54	chart (`le_iSup_basicOpen_of_sum_eq_one`). -/
    55	structure BasicOpenCoverData [IsAffineHom π] : Type (u + 1) where
    56	  /-- The chart-0 index. -/
    57	  J₀ : Type u
    58	  /-- The chart-1 index. -/
    59	  J₁ : Type u
    60	  /-- The chart-0 index is finite. -/
    61	  fintype₀ : Fintype J₀
    62	  /-- The chart-1 index is finite. -/
    63	  fintype₁ : Fintype J₁
    64	  /-- The chart-0 basic-open generators. -/
    65	  h₀ : J₀ → Γ(relCurve C B, (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀)
    66	  /-- The chart-1 basic-open generators. -/
    67	  h₁ : J₁ → Γ(relCurve C B, (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁)
    68	  /-- The chart-0 partition coefficients. -/
    69	  a₀ : J₀ → Γ(relCurve C B, (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀)
    70	  /-- The chart-1 partition coefficients. -/
    71	  a₁ : J₁ → Γ(relCurve C B, (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁)
    72	  /-- The chart-0 partition witness. -/
    73	  partition₀ : ∑ j : J₀, a₀ j * h₀ j = 1
    74	  /-- The chart-1 partition witness. -/
    75	  partition₁ : ∑ j : J₁, a₁ j * h₁ j = 1
    76	
    77	attribute [instance] BasicOpenCoverData.fintype₀ BasicOpenCoverData.fintype₁
    78	
    79	namespace BasicOpenCoverData
    80	
    81	variable {C B π} [IsAffineHom π] (D : BasicOpenCoverData C B π)
    82	
    83	/-- The gluing index of the datum, `J = J₀ ⊕ J₁`. -/
    84	abbrev index : Type u := D.J₀ ⊕ D.J₁
    85	
    86	/-- The pieces of the datum: the basic opens `D(h_j)` of the two pinned charts. -/
    87	noncomputable def pieces : D.index → (relCurve C B).Opens :=
    88	  Sum.elim (fun j => (relCurve C B).basicOpen (D.h₀ j))
    89	    (fun j => (relCurve C B).basicOpen (D.h₁ j))
    90	
    91	@[simp]
    92	lemma pieces_inl (j : D.J₀) :
    93	    D.pieces (Sum.inl j) = (relCurve C B).basicOpen (D.h₀ j) := rfl
    94	
    95	@[simp]
    96	lemma pieces_inr (j : D.J₁) :
    97	    D.pieces (Sum.inr j) = (relCurve C B).basicOpen (D.h₁ j) := rfl
    98	
    99	/-- The chart-0 pieces cover the pinned chart `V₀ᴮ`. -/
   100	lemma cover₀ : (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ ≤
   101	    ⨆ j : D.J₀, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (D.h₀ j) :=
   102	  le_iSup_basicOpen_of_sum_eq_one D.a₀ D.h₀ D.partition₀
   103	
   104	/-- The chart-1 pieces cover the pinned chart `V₁ᴮ`. -/
   105	lemma cover₁ : (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ ≤
   106	    ⨆ j : D.J₁, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (D.h₁ j) :=
   107	  le_iSup_basicOpen_of_sum_eq_one D.a₁ D.h₁ D.partition₁
   108	
   109	/-- The chart-0 generators, restricted to the overlap of the pinned charts. -/
   110	noncomputable def hInf (j : D.J₀) :
   111	    Γ(relCurve C B,
   112	      (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ ⊓ (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁) :=
   113	  (relCurve C B).resHom inf_le_left (D.h₀ j)
   114	
   115	/-- The restricted chart-0 pieces are subordinate to the pieces of the datum. -/
   116	lemma basicOpen_hInf_le (j : D.J₀) :
   117	    (relCurve C B).basicOpen (D.hInf j) ≤ D.pieces (Sum.inl j) := by
   118	  rw [hInf, Scheme.basicOpen_resHom, pieces_inl]
   119	  exact inf_le_right
   120	
   121	/-- The restricted chart-0 pieces cover the overlap of the pinned charts (the
   122	partition witness restricts to a partition witness). -/
   123	lemma coverInf : (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ ⊓ (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁
   124	    ≤ ⨆ j : D.J₀, (relCurve C B).basicOpen (D.hInf j) := by
   125	  refine le_iSup_basicOpen_of_sum_eq_one
   126	    (fun j => (relCurve C B).resHom inf_le_left (D.a₀ j)) D.hInf ?_
   127	  have hres := congrArg
   128	    ((relCurve C B).resHom (inf_le_left : (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ ⊓
   129	      (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ ≤ (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀))
   130	    D.partition₀
   131	  rw [map_sum, map_one] at hres
   132	  rw [← hres]
   133	  exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun j _ => (map_mul _ _ _).symm
   134	
   135	end BasicOpenCoverData
   136	
   137	/-- **The pinned cocycle datum over `B`** (worksheet §3.2, VERBATIM): the basic-open
   138	cover data of the two pinned charts together with transition units on the pairwise
   139	basic-open overlaps (with explicit inverse witnesses — `Units`) satisfying the cocycle
   140	identities in the overlap section rings (`Scheme.IsGluingCocycle`, including the
   141	normalization `g j j = 1`). This is the DAT-1 constructor input and the object RE-5
   142	descends. -/
   143	structure BasicOpenCocycleDatum [IsAffineHom π] : Type (u + 1) extends
   144	    BasicOpenCoverData C B π where
   145	  /-- The transition units on the pairwise piece overlaps. -/
   146	  unit : ∀ i j : toBasicOpenCoverData.index,
   147	    Γ(relCurve C B, toBasicOpenCoverData.pieces i ⊓ toBasicOpenCoverData.pieces j)ˣ
   148	  /-- The cocycle law. -/
   149	  isGluingCocycle : Scheme.IsGluingCocycle toBasicOpenCoverData.pieces unit
   150	
   151	namespace BasicOpenCocycleDatum
   152	
   153	variable {C B π} [IsAffineHom π] (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
   154	
   155	/-- **The glued sheaf of the datum**: the m-chart cocycle-glued sheaf of `B`-modules on
   156	the small Zariski site of the relative curve `C_B`. -/
   157	@[reducible] noncomputable def sheaf :
   158	    Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology ((relCurve C B : Scheme.{u}) : TopCat))
   159	      (ModuleCat.{u} B) :=
   160	  gluedSheaf B D.pieces D.unit
   161	
   162	/-- The quasi-coherence packaging of the datum's glued sheaf on the pinned chart
   163	`V₀ᴮ`, from the chart-0 family. -/
   164	noncomputable instance instQcohOn₀ :
   165	    Scheme.QcohOn D.sheaf (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ :=
   166	  gluedQcohOn B D.pieces D.unit D.isGluingCocycle (σ := Sum.inl) (h := D.h₀)
   167	    (fun _ => le_rfl) D.cover₀
   168	
   169	/-- The quasi-coherence packaging on the pinned chart `V₁ᴮ`, from the chart-1
   170	family. -/
   171	noncomputable instance instQcohOn₁ :
   172	    Scheme.QcohOn D.sheaf (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ :=
   173	  gluedQcohOn B D.pieces D.unit D.isGluingCocycle (σ := Sum.inr) (h := D.h₁)
   174	    (fun _ => le_rfl) D.cover₁
   175	
   176	/-- The quasi-coherence packaging on the overlap of the pinned charts, from the
   177	restricted chart-0 family (the subordinate-pieces interface). -/
   178	noncomputable instance instQcohOnInf :
   179	    Scheme.QcohOn D.sheaf
   180	      ((relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ ⊓ (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁) :=
   181	  gluedQcohOn B D.pieces D.unit D.isGluingCocycle
   182	    (σ := fun j : D.J₀ => Sum.inl j) (h := D.hInf)
   183	    (fun j => D.basicOpen_hInf_le j) D.coverInf
   184	
   185	/-- **The two-cover pair data of the datum's glued sheaf** at the pinned relative chart
   186	coordinates `t₀ᴮ, t₁ᴮ`: overlap-as-basic-open from the landed
   187	`relCover_fiberTwoCover_inf_eq_basicOpen₀/₁`, mutual inverse from the pulled-back
   188	`P1.chartCoord` relation `relFiberCoord_mul`. Its `pair` is the two-lattice pair of the
   189	datum's sheaf that the rigid engine consumes. -/
   190	noncomputable def pairData :
   191	    Scheme.TwoCoverPairData D.sheaf (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
   192	      (relCover C B (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ :=
   193	  gluedPairData B D.pieces D.unit
   194	    (fun _ _ _ => rfl) (fun _ _ _ => rfl)
   195	    (relFiberCoord₀ C B π) (relFiberCoord₁ C B π)
   196	    (relCover_fiberTwoCover_inf_eq_basicOpen₀ C B π)
   197	    (relCover_fiberTwoCover_inf_eq_basicOpen₁ C B π)
   198	    (relFiberCoord_mul C B π)
   199	
   200	end BasicOpenCocycleDatum

    11	/-!
    12	# Presented étale covers of an affine base
    13	
    14	A (singleton, affine) *étale cover* of `Spec A` is a faithfully flat étale `A`-algebra `B`.
    15	For the étale-sheafification (plus) construction of the relative Picard functor, the covers
    16	of a fixed base must form a *small* directed index: this file realizes them as **presented**
    17	covers — a number of variables `n` together with an ideal of `MvPolynomial (Fin n) A` whose
    18	quotient is étale over `A` with `Spec` mapping onto `Spec A`.  The type of presented covers
    19	of `A` lives in the same universe as `A`, while still capturing every étale cover up to
    20	isomorphism of the carrier (`Algebra.EtaleCover.of` and its accessor `ofEquiv`).
    21	
    22	Surjectivity of the spectrum map is recorded instead of faithful flatness because it is
    23	statable without flatness hypotheses; combined with flatness of étale algebras it *is*
    24	faithful flatness (`Module.FaithfullyFlat.of_comap_surjective`), and that instance is
    25	provided on the carrier.
    26	
    27	## Main declarations
    28	
    29	* `Algebra.EtaleCover A`: presented étale covers of `Spec A`, a `Type u` for `A : Type u`;
    30	  `E.Carrier` is the covering algebra, with `Algebra.Etale A E.Carrier` and
    31	  `Module.FaithfullyFlat A E.Carrier` instances.
    32	* `Algebra.EtaleCover.of B hB`: any étale `A`-algebra `B` (with surjective spectrum map)
    33	  underlies a presented cover, with carrier identification `Algebra.EtaleCover.ofEquiv`.
    34	* `Algebra.EtaleCover.Refines`: `E'` refines `E` when the covering spectrum of `E'` maps
    35	  to that of `E` over the base — a mere existence (`Prop`); the plus construction proves
    36	  independence of the chosen refinement map, so no choice of map is carried here.
    37	* `Algebra.EtaleCover.prod`: the common refinement `Spec (B ⊗[A] B')` of two covers, with
    38	  refinement witnesses `prodInl`/`prodInr` — directedness of the index
    39	  (`exists_refines_prod`).
    40	* `Algebra.EtaleCover.self`: the trivial cover `Spec A` itself, refined by every cover
    41	  (`refines_self`) — the base point of the index.
    42	* `Algebra.EtaleCover.baseChange`: the pulled-back cover along `A → A'`, with carrier
    43	  `A' ⊗[A] E.Carrier` (`baseChangeEquiv`) and the canonical `A`-algebra map
    44	  `baseChangeInclude` into it.
    45	* `Algebra.EtaleCover.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom`: over a field `K`, every cover
    46	  is refined by a finite separable field extension of `K` (single-factor refinement) —
    47	  field-extension covers are cofinal, the form the degree theory and Galois descent
    48	  consume; `Algebra.EtaleCover.ofField` packages such an extension as a cover.
    49	-/
    50	
    51	set_option autoImplicit false
    52	
    53	universe u
    54	
    55	open TensorProduct
    56	
    57	namespace Algebra
    58	
    59	/-- A presented étale cover of `Spec A`: a finite-variable polynomial presentation of an
    60	étale `A`-algebra whose spectrum maps onto `Spec A`.  Presentations keep the type of covers
    61	small (`Type u` for `A : Type u`), which is what makes the étale plus construction over
    62	these covers a legitimate colimit; the carrier-level content is recovered by
    63	`Algebra.EtaleCover.of`/`ofEquiv`. -/
    64	structure EtaleCover (A : Type u) [CommRing A] : Type u where
    65	  /-- The number of variables of the presentation. -/
    66	  n : ℕ
    67	  /-- The ideal of relations of the presentation. -/
    68	  ideal : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A)
    69	  /-- The presented algebra is étale over the base. -/
    70	  etale : Algebra.Etale A (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⧸ ideal)
    71	  /-- The spectrum of the presented algebra covers the spectrum of the base. -/
    72	  comap_surjective :
    73	    Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⧸ ideal)))
    74	
    75	namespace EtaleCover
    76	
    77	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    78	
    79	/-- The covering algebra presented by an étale cover. -/
    80	protected abbrev Carrier (E : EtaleCover A) : Type u :=
    81	  MvPolynomial (Fin E.n) A ⧸ E.ideal
    82	
    83	instance (E : EtaleCover A) : Algebra.Etale A E.Carrier :=
    84	  E.etale
    85	
    86	instance (E : EtaleCover A) : Module.FaithfullyFlat A E.Carrier :=
    87	  .of_comap_surjective E.comap_surjective
    88	
    89	/-! ## Constructors -/
    90	
    91	section constructors
    92	
    93	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.Etale A B]
    94	
    95	/-- Package an explicitly presented étale algebra with surjective spectrum map as a
    96	presented étale cover: the ideal of relations is the kernel of the presenting
    97	surjection. -/
    98	noncomputable def ofSurjective
    99	    (hB : Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A B)))
   100	    {n : ℕ} (f : MvPolynomial (Fin n) A →ₐ[A] B) (hf : Function.Surjective f) :
   101	    EtaleCover A where
   102	  n := n
   103	  ideal := RingHom.ker f
   104	  etale := .of_equiv (Ideal.quotientKerAlgEquivOfSurjective hf).symm
   105	  comap_surjective := by
   106	    haveI : Module.FaithfullyFlat A B := .of_comap_surjective hB
   107	    haveI : Module.FaithfullyFlat A (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⧸ RingHom.ker f) :=
   108	      .of_linearEquiv A B (Ideal.quotientKerAlgEquivOfSurjective hf).toLinearEquiv
   109	    exact PrimeSpectrum.comap_surjective_of_faithfullyFlat
   110	
   111	/-- The carrier of `ofSurjective` is the presented algebra. -/
   112	noncomputable def ofSurjectiveEquiv
   113	    (hB : Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A B)))
   114	    {n : ℕ} (f : MvPolynomial (Fin n) A →ₐ[A] B) (hf : Function.Surjective f) :
   115	    (ofSurjective hB f hf).Carrier ≃ₐ[A] B :=
   116	  Ideal.quotientKerAlgEquivOfSurjective hf
   117	
   118	/-- Any étale `A`-algebra whose spectrum covers `Spec A` underlies a presented étale
   119	cover.  The presentation is chosen (étale algebras are finitely presented, in particular
   120	finitely generated); the choice is harmless because consumers only ever use the carrier
   121	identification `ofEquiv`. -/
   122	noncomputable def of (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.Etale A B]
   123	    (hB : Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A B))) : EtaleCover A :=
   124	  ofSurjective hB
   125	    (Algebra.FiniteType.iff_quotient_mvPolynomial''.mp inferInstance).choose_spec.choose
   126	    (Algebra.FiniteType.iff_quotient_mvPolynomial''.mp inferInstance).choose_spec.choose_spec
   127	
   128	/-- The carrier of `of B hB` is `B` itself. -/
   129	noncomputable def ofEquiv (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.Etale A B]
   130	    (hB : Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A B))) :
   131	    (of B hB).Carrier ≃ₐ[A] B :=
   132	  ofSurjectiveEquiv hB _ _
   133	
   134	end constructors
   135	
   136	/-! ## Refinement and directedness -/
   137	
   138	/-- `E'` refines `E`: the covering spectrum of `E'` maps to that of `E` over `Spec A`,
   139	i.e. there is an `A`-algebra map from the carrier of `E` to that of `E'`.  This is a mere
   140	existence: the plus construction proves that the induced maps on descent classes do not
   141	depend on the chosen refinement map, so no map is carried here. -/
   142	def Refines (E' E : EtaleCover A) : Prop :=
   143	  Nonempty (E.Carrier →ₐ[A] E'.Carrier)
   144	
   145	theorem refines_refl (E : EtaleCover A) : E.Refines E :=
   146	  ⟨AlgHom.id A E.Carrier⟩
   147	
   148	theorem Refines.trans {E E' E'' : EtaleCover A} (h : E''.Refines E') (h' : E'.Refines E) :
   149	    E''.Refines E := by
   150	  obtain ⟨f⟩ := h
   151	  obtain ⟨g⟩ := h'
   152	  exact ⟨f.comp g⟩
   153	
   154	/-- The common refinement of two covers: `Spec` of the tensor product of the carriers,
   155	i.e. the fiber product of the covering spectra over the base. -/
   156	noncomputable def prod (E E' : EtaleCover A) : EtaleCover A :=
   157	  haveI : Algebra.Etale A (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier) :=
   158	    Algebra.Etale.comp A E.Carrier (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier)
   159	  haveI : Module.FaithfullyFlat A (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier) :=
   160	    Module.FaithfullyFlat.trans A E.Carrier (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier)
   161	  .of (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier) PrimeSpectrum.comap_surjective_of_faithfullyFlat
   162	
   163	/-- The carrier of the common refinement is the tensor product of the carriers. -/
   164	noncomputable def prodEquiv (E E' : EtaleCover A) :
   165	    (E.prod E').Carrier ≃ₐ[A] E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier :=
   166	  haveI : Algebra.Etale A (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier) :=
   167	    Algebra.Etale.comp A E.Carrier (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier)
   168	  haveI : Module.FaithfullyFlat A (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier) :=
   169	    Module.FaithfullyFlat.trans A E.Carrier (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier)
   170	  ofEquiv (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier) PrimeSpectrum.comap_surjective_of_faithfullyFlat
   171	
   172	/-- The first refinement map of the common refinement. -/
   173	noncomputable def prodInl (E E' : EtaleCover A) : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] (E.prod E').Carrier :=
   174	  ((E.prodEquiv E').symm.toAlgHom).comp Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft
   175	
   176	/-- The second refinement map of the common refinement. -/
   177	noncomputable def prodInr (E E' : EtaleCover A) : E'.Carrier →ₐ[A] (E.prod E').Carrier :=
   178	  ((E.prodEquiv E').symm.toAlgHom).comp Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight
   179	
   180	/-- Combine refinement maps out of the two factors into one out of the common
   181	refinement (the universal property of the fiber product of the covering spectra). -/
   182	noncomputable def prodLift {E E' F : EtaleCover A} (f : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
   183	    (g : E'.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) : (E.prod E').Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier :=
   184	  (Algebra.TensorProduct.lift f g fun _ _ => Commute.all _ _).comp
   185	    (E.prodEquiv E').toAlgHom
   186	
   187	@[simp]
   188	theorem prodLift_comp_prodInl {E E' F : EtaleCover A} (f : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
   189	    (g : E'.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) : (prodLift f g).comp (E.prodInl E') = f := by
   190	  ext x
   191	  simp [prodLift, prodInl]
   192	
   193	@[simp]
   194	theorem prodLift_comp_prodInr {E E' F : EtaleCover A} (f : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
   195	    (g : E'.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) : (prodLift f g).comp (E.prodInr E') = g := by
   196	  ext x
   197	  simp [prodLift, prodInr]
   198

import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.GluedSheafQcoh

/-!
# QcohOn for the m-chart glued sheaf (DAT-1, stage 1b, assembly)

The (P2) localization axioms and the quasi-coherence packaging of the glued sheaf
`gluedSheaf k U g` on a chart `V` under the **trivializing-family interface**
(`informal/spec-dat-1.md` decision (D3), in subordinate form): a finite family of basic
opens `D(h i)` (`h : ι → Γ(X, V)`) covering `V`, each contained in a gluing piece
`U (σ i)` (`hP : D(h i) ≤ U (σ i)` — containment, not equality, so that restricted
families serve smaller charts such as the pinned overlap).

* `exists_gluedRes_eq_gluedQsmul_pow` — **(P2) denominator clearing**: per-piece
  clearing (`IsAffineOpen.exists_res_eq_pow_mul`), finite uniformization of the
  exponent, defect annihilation on the affine double overlaps
  (`IsAffineOpen.exists_pow_mul_eq_zero_of_res_eq_zero`), regluing in the sheaf, and a
  local comparison through `gluedSubmodule_ext`.
* `exists_gluedQsmul_pow_eq_zero` — **(P2) defect annihilation**: per-piece
  annihilation, finite uniformization, `gluedSubmodule_ext` against `0`.
* `gluedQcohOn` — the assembled packaging `Scheme.QcohOn (gluedSheaf k U g) V`
  (a `def`; keyed `instance`s are declared only at the pinned datum, stage 1d).
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite TopologicalSpace

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

section Assembly

variable (k : Type u) [CommRing k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (.of k))]

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule

variable {J : Type u} (U : J → X.Opens) (g : ∀ i j : J, Γ(X, U i ⊓ U j)ˣ)
variable {V : X.Opens} {ι : Type u} [Finite ι] {σ : ι → J} {h : ι → Γ(X, V)}

     9	/-!
    10	# The shared plus-class field collapse (DAT-B B-5 fibre collapse / B-4 gap-1 collapse)
    11	
    12	This is the **shared plus-class collapse lemma** flagged by `w4-datb-worksheet.md` §5
    13	risk 6 and by the B-4 landing note I-0252 ("state it once as a named lemma with a
    14	characterizing property … both consume it"): a plus class of the one-step étale-plus
    15	Picard group over a *field* becomes an honest relative-Picard class after base change to a
    16	suitable finite separable field extension.
    17	
    18	Over a field `K`, a plus class `p : PicEtAff C K` is `PicEtAff.mk E x` for a presented
    19	étale cover `E` of `Spec K` and a descent class `x` (`Picard/PicEtAff.lean`).  Field
    20	cofinality (`Algebra.EtaleCover.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom`,
    21	`Algebra/EtaleCover.lean` — étale covers of a field are refined by finite separable field
    22	extensions) supplies a finite separable `L/K` together with a `K`-algebra map
    23	`ℓ : E.Carrier →ₐ[K] L`.  Base-changing `E` to `L` yields a cover with an `L`-point, so the
    24	base-changed descent class is, by the descent/cocycle condition (`relPicAlgMap_congr`), the
    25	tautological datum of an honest class: `PicEtAff.map C L p` is the plus-unit of the
    26	relative-Picard class `relPicAlgMap ℓ x` on `C_L` (`PicEtAff.unit C L …`).
    27	
    28	## Main results
    29	
    30	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_of_algHom` — the collapse: `mk C E x`
    31	  restricted over a finite separable `L/K` (via a `K`-algebra map `ℓ` of the cover
    32	  carrier) is `PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicAlgMap ℓ x)`.
    33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_relPicMk_of_algHom` — the same with the honest
    34	  class presented as `relPicMk` of a Čech Picard class `M` on `C_L`, the form the degree
    35	  seam (`degAt_of_affineEquiv_eq_unit_relPicMk`) and the shifted-datum extraction
    36	  (`exists_cechPicClass_eq`) consume.
    37	
    38	The finite separable `L` with `ℓ : E.Carrier →ₐ[K] L` is supplied by field cofinality
    39	(`Algebra.EtaleCover.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom`).  Both statements take the tower
    40	`k → K → L` as clean instance hypotheses — the campaign-idiomatic fibre-extension form
    41	(cf. `Picard/DivSchemeSeed.lean`).  A consumer must instantiate `L` with a well-behaved
    42	`Algebra k L` (a native tower); a `RingHom.toAlgebra`-composite `letI` triggers the
    43	two-level-tower diamond of I-0236 when `PicEtAff.map C L` unfolds the base-changed carrier
    44	(a genuine `whnf` non-termination, verified this pass — see the landing note).
    45	
    46	The statements carry **no** hypotheses on the curve `C.hom` (they are purely about the
    47	plus construction), so they are available to every consumer of the plus group.
    48	-/
