    63	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    64	
    65	set_option maxHeartbeats 800000 in
    66	-- The base-changed étale carrier is a quotient of a polynomial ring; the descent
    67	-- naturality defeq through it is heavy, so bump the budget for this declaration.
    68	/-- **The plus-class collapse at an explicit refinement `ℓ` into a finite separable
    69	extension** — the honest math heart of the collapse, with the extension `L` and its
    70	tower a hypothesis (so no composite-algebra `letI` is forced through the base-changed
    71	carrier).  For a descent class `x` on a cover `E` of `K` and a `K`-algebra map
    72	`ℓ : E.Carrier →ₐ[K] L`, the plus class `mk C E x` restricts over `L` to the plus-unit of
    73	the honest relative-Picard class `relPicAlgMap ℓ x` on `C_L`.
    74	
    75	Route: `map_mk` reads the restriction as `mk (E.baseChange L) (descentBaseChange x)`;
    76	`unit_eq_mk` reads the target unit on the same cover; the descent condition
    77	(`relPicAlgMap_congr`, applied to `baseChangeInclude` and `ofId ∘ ℓ`) identifies the two
    78	descent classes through `descentBaseChange_coe`. -/
    79	theorem PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_of_algHom {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    80	    [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra K L] [IsScalarTower k K L]
    81	    {E : Algebra.EtaleCover K} (x : descentClasses C E) (ℓ : E.Carrier →ₐ[K] L) :
    82	    PicEtAff.map C L (PicEtAff.mk C E x)
    83	      = PicEtAff.unit C L
    84	          (relPicAlgMap C (ℓ.restrictScalars k) (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier))) := by
    85	  have hval : (descentBaseChange C L E x : relPic C (overSpec k (E.baseChange L).Carrier))
    86	      = relPicAlgMap C ((Algebra.ofId L (E.baseChange L).Carrier).restrictScalars k)
    87	          (relPicAlgMap C (ℓ.restrictScalars k) (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier))) := by
    88	    rw [descentBaseChange_coe, ← relPicAlgMap_comp]
    89	    exact relPicAlgMap_congr C (E.baseChangeInclude L)
    90	      (((Algebra.ofId L (E.baseChange L).Carrier).restrictScalars K).comp ℓ) x.2
    91	  rw [PicEtAff.map_mk,
    92	    PicEtAff.unit_eq_mk C (E.baseChange L)
    93	      (relPicAlgMap C (ℓ.restrictScalars k) (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)))]
    94	  exact congrArg (PicEtAff.mk C (E.baseChange L)) (Subtype.ext hval)
    95	
    96	/-- **The shared plus-class field collapse, Čech form** (`w4-datb` §1.2 step 1; B-4 gap-1).
    97	The honest class `relPicAlgMap ℓ x` of `PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_of_algHom` is presented as
    98	`relPicMk` of a Čech Picard class `M` on `C_L` — the form the degree seam
    99	(`degAt_of_affineEquiv_eq_unit_relPicMk`) and the shifted-datum extraction
   100	(`exists_cechPicClass_eq`) consume. -/
   101	theorem PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_relPicMk_of_algHom {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
   102	    [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra K L] [IsScalarTower k K L]
   103	    {E : Algebra.EtaleCover K} (x : descentClasses C E) (ℓ : E.Carrier →ₐ[K] L) :
   104	    ∃ M : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.CechPic,
   105	      PicEtAff.map C L (PicEtAff.mk C E x)
   106	        = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M) := by
   107	  obtain ⟨M, hM⟩ := relPicMk_surjective C (overSpec k L)
   108	    (relPicAlgMap C (ℓ.restrictScalars k) (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)))
   109	  exact ⟨M, by rw [PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_of_algHom C x ℓ, hM]⟩
   110	
   111	end AlgebraicGeometry

     8	/-!
     9	# The unconditional splitting of a plus class over a field (CHART-U(a), input 1)
    10	
    11	`informal/w4-datb-worksheet.md` §1.2 step 1 and `informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md` §3.3 both
    12	open with the same move, and both treat it as a step of a longer argument:
    13	
    14	> restrict along `t`; a plus class over `κ(t)` is `PicEtAff.mk E x`; étale field-cofinality
    15	> produces a finite separable `L/κ(t)` over which the class is an honest Čech class.
    16	
    17	This file makes that move a **named, unconditional theorem** rather than a step, because it
    18	is consumed at three separate places (the split predicate `IsSplitWitness`, the coverage
    19	theorem COV-1, and the degree seam) and because its statement is exactly the *witness-free*
    20	half of `IsSplitWitness`: every plus class over a field becomes an honest Čech class over
    21	some finite separable extension.  Nothing here mentions a witness divisor, `H¹`, `θ`, `Σ`,
    22	`divRep` or a certificate.
    23	
    24	## Why this is worth isolating
    25	
    26	`IsSplitWitness C μ` (`Picard/Pic0ChartLocus.lean:148`) is an existential over a *tuple*: the
    27	extension `L`, its four instances, the presenting Čech class `M`, and then the witness
    28	divisor.  Read naively, a consumer proving membership of `chartLocus` has to produce all of
    29	them at once, and a consumer *using* membership has to destructure all of them.  But the
    30	first six components exist for **every** class, with no hypothesis at all — that is
    31	`exists_splitting_of_picEt` below.  So the honest content of `IsSplitWitness` is only the
    32	witness clause *at* a splitting, and the two readings are related by
    33	`isSplitWitness_iff_exists_splitting_witness`.
    34	
    35	That matters for the lane order: COV-1 (dat-b §1.2) can produce its splitting *before* it
    36	knows anything about `h⁰`/`h¹`, choose `m` at that field (§1.2 step 3, where the uniform
    37	bound genuinely does not exist), and only then run the drop.  Without this separation the
    38	`m`-choice and the splitting choice are entangled inside one `∃`.
    39	
    40	## Main declarations
    41	
    42	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_splitting_of_picEtAff` — **every plus class over a field is an
    43	  honest Čech class over some finite separable extension.**  Unconditional; no witness.
    44	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_splitting_of_picEt` — the same in the `picEt` spelling, which is
    45	  the one `IsSplitWitness` is stated against.
    46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isSplitWitness_iff_exists_splitting_witness` — the two readings agree:
    47	  `IsSplitWitness` is exactly "some splitting carries a witness".  Its `.mpr` is also the
    48	  introduction rule; see the closing note for why no positional constructor lemma exists.
    49	-/

    76	
    77	set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000 in
    78	-- The presentation lives over the base-changed étale carrier, and closing the existential
    79	-- unifies its `Algebra k L` (the derived composite) against the goal's through that carrier
    80	-- — the same heavy defeq `PicEtAffFieldCollapse.lean` budgets 800000 for.
    81	/-- **Every plus class over a field is an honest Čech class over some finite separable
    82	extension** (`w4-datb` §1.2 step 1, `w4-datc` §3.3 — the first move of both, here
    83	unconditional and witness-free).
    84	
    85	Given `μ : picEt C (overSpec k K)`, there is a finite separable `L/K` and a Čech Picard
    86	class `M` on `C_L` with `μ|_L = relPicMk M` as plus classes.
    87	
    88	The three steps, each a landed brick:
    89	
    90	1. `picEtAffineEquiv` (`Picard/PicEt.lean:235`) reads `μ` in `PicEtAff C K`, where by
    91	   `PicEtAff.ind` it is `PicEtAff.mk E x` for a presented étale cover `E` of `K` and a
    92	   descent class `x`;
    93	2. étale field-cofinality — `Algebra.EtaleCover.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom`
    94	   (`Algebra/EtaleCover.lean:287`) — refines `E` by a finite separable field `L/K`,
    95	   i.e. supplies `ℓ : E.Carrier →ₐ[K] L`.  This is the step that uses that `K` is a
    96	   *field*: over a general base an étale cover has no such refinement;
    97	3. `PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_relPicMk_of_algHom` (`Picard/PicEtAffFieldCollapse.lean:101`)
    98	   converts the refinement into the presentation.
    99	
   100	The `k`-algebra structure on `L` and the tower `k → K → L` are *derived*, not chosen: they
   101	are the composite `algebraMap K L ∘ algebraMap k K`, exactly as `degAffFieldAlgebraBase`
   102	(`Picard/DegreeZero.lean:229`) does it.  Constructing them here rather than demanding them
   103	of the caller is the whole ergonomic point — a caller who has only `K` cannot produce them,
   104	since `L` does not exist until step 2. -/
   105	theorem exists_splitting_of_picEtAff (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   106	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   107	    {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
   108	    (a : PicEtAff C K) :
   109	    ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L) (_ : Algebra K L)
   110	        (_ : IsScalarTower k K L) (_ : Module.Finite K L) (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable K L)
   111	        (M : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CechPic),
   112	      PicEtAff.map C L a = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M) := by
   113	  -- (1) read `a` as a plus class on a presented cover
   114	  induction a using PicEtAff.ind with
   115	  | mk E x =>
   116	    -- (2) refine the cover by a finite separable field
   117	    obtain ⟨L, hLfield, hLalg, hLfin, hLsep, ⟨ℓ⟩⟩ := E.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom
   118	    letI := hLfield
   119	    letI := hLalg
   120	    letI := hLfin
   121	    letI := hLsep
   122	    -- the `k`-structure and the tower are the composite, not a choice
   123	    letI hkL : Algebra k L := ((algebraMap K L).comp (algebraMap k K)).toAlgebra
   124	    haveI htow : IsScalarTower k K L := .of_algebraMap_eq fun _ => rfl
   125	    -- FORGET the composite's VALUE before going further (I-0161-adjacent hazard, measured
   126	    -- this session).  Keeping it transparent makes the final `exact` substitute a composite
   127	    -- algebra term for the existential's variable, and every `overSpec k L` /
   128	    -- `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left` in the goal is then rechecked against a differently-spelled
   129	    -- instance — that defeq does not terminate inside 1600000 heartbeats.  `htow` is a
   130	    -- `have`, so it has already forgotten the value it was proved from; nothing downstream
   131	    -- needs it.
   132	    clear_value hkL
   133	    -- (3) the refinement is the presentation
   134	    obtain ⟨M, hM⟩ := PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_relPicMk_of_algHom C x ℓ
   135	    exact ⟨L, hLfield, hkL, hLalg, htow, hLfin, hLsep, M, hM⟩
   136	
   137	variable (C) in
   138	/-- **The splitting theorem in the `picEt` spelling** — the form every consumer of
   139	`IsSplitWitness` meets, since the split predicate is stated on
   140	`PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K μ)`.  Immediate from
   141	`exists_splitting_of_picEtAff` at `a := picEtAffineEquiv C K μ`; kept separate so that the
   142	heavy elaboration of the previous theorem is not re-run through the affine comparison. -/
   143	theorem exists_splitting_of_picEt {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
   144	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K)) :
   145	    ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L) (_ : Algebra K L)
   146	        (_ : IsScalarTower k K L) (_ : Module.Finite K L) (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable K L)
   147	        (M : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CechPic),
   148	      PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K μ)
   149	        = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M) :=
   150	  exists_splitting_of_picEtAff C (picEtAffineEquiv C K μ)

   152	/-! ## The two readings of `IsSplitWitness` -/
   153	
   154	variable (C) in
   155	/-- **`IsSplitWitness` is exactly "some splitting carries a witness"** — the two readings of
   156	the (a-amendment) agree.
   157	
   158	The forward direction is destructuring.  The reverse is `isSplitWitness_of_splitting`.  The
   159	point of stating it as an `iff` is that the *left* side is the definition consumers meet and
   160	the *right* side separates the two independent choices (which extension; which witness),
   161	which is what makes the COV-1 lane order of `w4-datb` §1.2 legal: the splitting is fixed at
   162	step 1, the witness only at step 5. -/
   163	theorem isSplitWitness_iff_exists_splitting_witness {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
   164	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K)) :
   165	    IsSplitWitness C μ
   166	      ↔ ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L) (_ : Algebra K L)
   167	          (_ : IsScalarTower k K L) (_ : Module.Finite K L) (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable K L)
   168	          (M : (relCurve C L).CechPic),
   169	        (PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K μ)
   170	            = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M))
   171	          ∧ ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor,
   172	              Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W = M
   173	                ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
   174	                    ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1) :=
   175	  Iff.rfl

   177	/-! ## A note on the intro rule — SUPERSEDED, and the correction matters
   178	
   179	**The intro rule EXISTS.** It is `isSplitWitness_of_presenting_witness`
   180	(`Picard/Pic0ChartTwistSplit.lean`), it elaborates at the default heartbeat budget, and its
   181	`L := K` case — the one this note's earlier version called out as wanted but unreachable — is
   182	a one-liner there.  Read that theorem's docstring, not this paragraph, for the current state.
   183	
   184	What this note originally recorded, and what remains TRUE: an `isSplitWitness_of_splitting`
   185	handing all twelve components to **one anonymous constructor** does not elaborate.
   186	`IsSplitWitness` mixes the two spellings of the base-changed curve —
   187	`(relCurve C L).CechPic` for the presenting class, `((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor` for
   188	the witness divisor — so a single tuple makes Lean unify the seven instance slots *while `L` is
   189	still a metavariable*, re-checking those carriers on each attempted assignment.  `refine`
   190	instead of `exact`, pre-bundling the witness clause, normalising either spelling, and routing
   191	through the `iff` are all the same shape, and all of them time out.
   192	
   193	What it got wrong was the conclusion drawn from that: it read "the tuple is too expensive" as
   194	"there is no introduction rule", and proposed restating `IsSplitWitness` with one spelling —
   195	a refactor of a definition co-signed in `w4-datb` §1.6.  The actual fix is tactic-level:
   196	**stage the existentials.**  Eight `refine Exists.intro x ?_`s fix `L` at the first step, after
   197	which every later component is checked against a closed type and the two spellings never race.
   198	
   199	So the corrected rule is not "prefer `Iff.rfl` plus `.mpr`" but: *a deep existential over
   200	types-carrying-instances must have its intros staged, not bundled.*  The diagnosis above is
   201	not refuted by this — it is precisely why staging works. -/

    14	# FLV-4 — the class form and the remaining witnesses
    15	
    16	The final brick of the Wave-4 fibrewise-large-twist-vanishing campaign
    17	(`informal/w4-flv-worksheet.md`, sub-brick FLV-4). It carries three obligations left open by
    18	the FLV-2+3 landing (the vanishing headline `FLVVanishing.lean`):
    19	
    20	## 1. The surjectivity witness (`0 < deg (fiberWeilDivisor π)` unconditionally)
    21	
    22	`AlgebraicGeometry.surjective_of_isFinite_of_isDominant`: a finite dominant morphism is
    23	surjective (a closed map with dense range hits everything). Feeding the surjection the
    24	`ℙ¹`-point `[1 : 0]` (`P1.exists_mem_chartOpen_zero_notMem_one`, the origin of the chart
    25	`D₊(X₀)` off the chart `D₊(X₁)`) produces a fiber point `x₀ ∈ V₀ ∖ V₁`, which discharges the
    26	pole-existence witness of `AlgebraicGeometry.fiberWeilDivisor_deg_pos_of_notMem_chart₁`
    27	unconditionally: `AlgebraicGeometry.zero_lt_deg_fiberWeilDivisor`, `0 < deg F`.
    28	
    29	## 2. The class form (`informal/w4-flv-worksheet.md` §§1.2, 2.5)
    30	
    31	`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_one_le_classDeg_of_isFinite_toP1`: for a
    32	finite dominant `π : Y ⟶ ℙ¹` and any Čech Picard classes `l`, `θ` with `1 ≤ classDeg θ`, the
    33	degree-one cohomology of `𝒪(D)` vanishes for **every** divisor `D` of class `l · θⁿ`, for all
    34	large `n`. The reduction of the worksheet §2.5, in the simplified `m = m₀` form:
    35	
    36	* run FLV-fiber (`subsingleton_hModule_divisorSheaf_one_of_isFinite_toP1`) on a divisor `D₀`
    37	  realizing `l`: `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(D₀ + m₀·F))`, `F` the fiber divisor, `d' := deg F ≥ 1`;
    38	* for `n` large, the residual class `θⁿ · (𝒪(F))⁻ᵐ⁰` has degree `≥ 1 − χ(𝒪)`, so the Riemann
    39	  inequality (`riemann_inequality`) gives a nonzero global section, hence an **effective**
    40	  witness `E` of that class (`exists_effective_of_picClass`);
    41	* `D₀ + m₀·F + E` is in class `l · θⁿ`; peeling `E` point-by-point transports `Subsingleton`
    42	  up the landed dévissage surjections (`peel_effective`, from `Sheaf.HModule.surjective_map_f`);
    43	* witness-independence (W6-lite `subsingleton_hModule_one_of_picClass_eq`) upgrades the single
    44	  witness `D₀ + m₀·F + E` to every `D` of the class.
    45	
    46	The rank corollary `AlgebraicGeometry.h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one` records the
    47	CBC-3 anchor `h⁰(𝒪(D)) = deg D + χ(𝒪)` under the vanishing.
    48	
    49	Both statements above take the finite dominant map as an explicit hypothesis, matching the shape
    50	of the landed FLV-fiber `subsingleton_hModule_divisorSheaf_one_of_isFinite_toP1`. The curve layer
    51	`C_K` satisfies every abstract-bundle instance, so a consumer holding a finite dominant
    52	`π : C_K ⟶ ℙ¹` applies the class form directly.
    53	
    54	## 3. Frontier: the dominance discharge for the *constructed* map
    55	
    56	Specializing the class form to the curve layer with **no** external map hypothesis would require
    57	`IsDominant` for the `π` produced by `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.MapToP1.exists_isFinite_toP1`. That
    58	map is dominant (its construction sends the generic point to the generic point via transcendence),

    62	generic), which lives outside this brick's write scope (the landed `Curve/` files). Deferred; the
    63	consumer supplies `[IsDominant π]` with the finite map it already constructs for the fiber
    64	geometry.

    84	/-- The divisor-bound comparison at a point reduces to the pointwise coefficient comparison in
    85	`ℤ`: `divisorBound A ≤ divisorBound B ↔ coeffAt A ≤ coeffAt B`. (Public re-derivation of the

    87	lemma divisorBound_le_iff {A B : X.CurveDivisor} {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) :

    89	      coeffAt hx A ≤ coeffAt hx B := by

    99	variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]

   103	/-- The Čech Picard class of a multiple divisor is the power of the class:
   104	`𝒪(n·D) = 𝒪(D)ⁿ`. -/
   105	lemma picClass_nsmul (D : X.CurveDivisor) (n : ℕ) :
   106	    CurveDivisor.picClass K (n • D) = CurveDivisor.picClass K D ^ n := by
   107	  induction n with
   108	  | zero => rw [zero_nsmul, pow_zero, CurveDivisor.picClass_zero]
   109	  | succ n ih => rw [succ_nsmul, CurveDivisor.picClass_add, ih, pow_succ]
   110	
   111	variable [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
   112	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 1)]
   113	
   114	/-- The degree of a power of a Čech Picard class is the multiple of the degree:
   115	`classDeg (Lⁿ) = n · classDeg L`. -/
   116	lemma classDeg_pow (L : X.CechPic) (n : ℕ) :
   117	    classDeg K (L ^ n) = n * classDeg K L := by
   118	  induction n with
   119	  | zero => rw [pow_zero, classDeg_one, Nat.cast_zero, zero_mul]
   120	  | succ n ih => rw [pow_succ, classDeg_mul, ih, Nat.cast_succ]; ring
   121	
   122	end ClassArith

   124	/-! ## The surjectivity witness (`0 < deg F`) -/
   125	
   126	section Witness
   127	
   128	/-- **A `ℙ¹`-point off the chart `D₊(X₁)`.** The origin `[1 : 0]` of the chart `D₊(X₀)`: the
   129	prime containing the chart coordinate `X₁/X₀` (a non-unit — it is the polynomial variable),
   130	whose image lies in `D₊(X₀)` but not in `D₊(X₁)`. This is the point whose (nonempty, by
   131	surjectivity) fiber supplies the pole witness of the fiber divisor. -/
   132	theorem exists_mem_chartOpen_zero_notMem_one (k : Type u) [Field k] :
   133	    ∃ z : P1 k, z ∈ P1.chartOpen k 0 ∧ z ∉ P1.chartOpen k 1 := by
   134	  have hpre : (P1.chartι k 0) ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 1
   135	      = PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen (P1.chartCoord k 0 1) := by
   136	    change (Proj.awayι (homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k) (X 0) (P1.X_mem k 0) one_pos)
   137	        ⁻¹ᵁ Proj.basicOpen (homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k) (X 1) = _
   138	    rw [Proj.awayι_preimage_basicOpen (homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k)
   139	        (P1.X_mem k 0) one_pos (P1.X_mem k 1) one_pos,
   140	      P1.isLocalizationElem_X_eq k 0 1]
   141	  have hnu : ¬ IsUnit (P1.chartCoord k 0 1) := by
   142	    intro h
   143	    have h2 := h.map (P1.awayAlgEquiv k P1.fin_zero_ne_one)
   144	    rw [P1.awayAlgEquiv_chartCoord] at h2
   145	    exact Polynomial.not_isUnit_X h2
   146	  have hspan : Ideal.span {P1.chartCoord k 0 1} ≠ ⊤ := by
   147	    rw [Ne, Ideal.span_singleton_eq_top]; exact hnu
   148	  obtain ⟨M, hM, hle⟩ := Ideal.exists_le_maximal _ hspan
   149	  have hpmem : P1.chartCoord k 0 1 ∈ M := hle (Ideal.mem_span_singleton_self _)
   150	  refine ⟨(P1.chartι k 0).base ⟨M, hM.isPrime⟩, ?_, ?_⟩
   151	  · rw [← P1.opensRange_chartι k 0]
   152	    exact ⟨⟨M, hM.isPrime⟩, rfl⟩
   153	  · intro hz
   154	    have hmem : (⟨M, hM.isPrime⟩ :
   155	        PrimeSpectrum (Away (homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k) (X 0)))
   156	        ∈ (P1.chartι k 0) ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen k 1 := hz
   157	    rw [hpre] at hmem
   158	    exact (PrimeSpectrum.mem_basicOpen _ _).mp hmem hpmem
   159	
   160	/-- **A finite dominant morphism is surjective.** Finiteness makes `π` a closed map, so its
   161	range is closed; dominance makes the range dense; a closed dense set is everything. -/
   162	theorem surjective_of_isFinite_of_isDominant {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (π : X ⟶ Y)
   163	    [IsFinite π] [IsDominant π] : Function.Surjective π.base := by
   164	  have hclosed : IsClosed (Set.range π.base) := π.isClosedMap.isClosed_range
   165	  haveI : Surjective π := surjective_of_isDominant_of_isClosed_range π hclosed
   166	  exact π.surjective
   167	
   168	variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral Y]
   169	  [Y.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
   170	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
   171	  [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
   172	  [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
   173	
   174	/-- **The pole-existence witness, unconditional.** For a **finite** dominant `π : Y ⟶ ℙ¹`, the
   175	fiber divisor `F = fiberWeilDivisor π` has strictly positive degree: surjectivity of `π` (finite
   176	dominant) produces a point `x₀` over `[1 : 0] ∈ V₀ ∖ V₁`, discharging the fiber witness of
   177	`AlgebraicGeometry.fiberWeilDivisor_deg_pos_of_notMem_chart₁`. This is the FLV-4 obligation that
   178	frees the fibrewise vanishing from its pole-existence hypothesis. -/
   179	theorem zero_lt_deg_fiberWeilDivisor (π : Y ⟶ P1 K) [IsFinite π] [IsDominant π] :
   180	    0 < CurveDivisor.deg K (fiberWeilDivisor π) := by
   181	  obtain ⟨z, hz0, hz1⟩ := exists_mem_chartOpen_zero_notMem_one K
   182	  obtain ⟨x₀, hx₀⟩ := surjective_of_isFinite_of_isDominant π z
   183	  have hxV₀ : x₀ ∈ fiberChart₀ π := by
   184	    change π.base x₀ ∈ P1.chartOpen K 0; rw [hx₀]; exact hz0
   185	  have hxV₁ : x₀ ∉ fiberChart₁ π := by
   186	    change ¬ π.base x₀ ∈ P1.chartOpen K 1; rw [hx₀]; exact hz1
   187	  have hx₀η : x₀ ≠ genericPoint Y := fun h =>
   188	    hxV₁ (by rw [h]; exact (genericPoint_mem_preimage_inf π).2)
   189	  exact fiberWeilDivisor_deg_pos_of_notMem_chart₁ π hx₀η hxV₀ hxV₁
   190	
   191	end Witness

   193	/-! ## The effective witness -/
   194	
   195	section Effective
   196	
   197	variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
   198	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
   199	  [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
   200	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
   201	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 1)]
   202	
   203	/-- **An effective witness of a class of large degree.** If a Weil divisor `W` has
   204	`1 ≤ deg W + χ(𝒪)` then its Čech Picard class is realized by an **effective** divisor. The
   205	Riemann inequality (`riemann_inequality`) forces a nonzero global section `f` of `𝒪(W)`, i.e.
   206	`f ∈ K(X)ˣ` with `W + div f ≥ 0`; that shift is effective and of the same class
   207	(`CurveDivisor.picClass_divOf`). -/
   208	lemma exists_effective_of_picClass (W : X.CurveDivisor)
   209	    (hW : 1 ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K W + Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K)) :
   210	    ∃ E : X.CurveDivisor, 0 ≤ E ∧ CurveDivisor.picClass K E = CurveDivisor.picClass K W := by
   211	  -- `h⁰(𝒪(W)) ≥ 1`, so `H⁰` is nontrivial.
   212	  have hfr : 0 < Module.finrank K (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K W) 0) := by
   213	    have h1 : (1 : ℤ) ≤ (Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K W) : ℤ) :=
   214	      le_trans hW (riemann_inequality K W)
   215	    have : 0 < Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K W) := by omega
   216	    exact this
   217	  haveI : Nontrivial (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K W) 0) :=
   218	    Module.nontrivial_of_finrank_pos hfr
   219	  -- a nonzero global section `g ∈ 𝒪(W)(⊤) ⊆ K(X)`.
   220	  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := exists_ne (0 : Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K W) 0)
   221	  set s := (Sheaf.HModule.linearEquiv₀ (Opens.grothendieckTopology (X : TopCat))
   222	    (isTerminalTop : IsTerminal (⊤ : X.Opens)) (X.divisorSheaf K W)) t with hs
   223	  have hsne : s ≠ 0 := by
   224	    rw [hs]; exact (LinearEquiv.map_ne_zero_iff _).mpr ht
   225	  set g : X.functionField := divisorVal K s with hg
   226	  have hgmem : g ∈ divisorSections K W ⊤ := divisorVal_mem K s
   227	  have hgne : g ≠ 0 := by
   228	    intro h
   229	    exact hsne (divisorSection_ext K
   230	      (show divisorVal K s = divisorVal K (0 : _) from by rw [← hg, h]; rfl))
   231	  -- the unit `u` and the effective shift.
   232	  set u : X.functionFieldˣ := Units.mk0 g hgne with hu
   233	  have huval : (u : X.functionField) = g := rfl
   234	  refine ⟨W + Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) u, ?_, ?_⟩
   235	  · -- effectivity: `coeffAt (W + div u) ≥ 0` from the pole bound
   236	    refine Finsupp.le_def.mpr (fun p => ?_)
   237	    change (0 : ℤ) ≤ coeffAt p.2 (W + Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) u)
   238	    have htop : ((⊤ : X.Opens) : Set X).Nonempty := ⟨genericPoint X, trivial⟩
   239	    have hb := (mem_divisorSections_of_nonempty K htop).mp hgmem p.1 p.2 trivial
   240	    rw [← huval, Scheme.ord_val_eq K u p.2, divisorBound_le_iff p.2,
   241	      CurveDivisor.coeffAt_neg] at hb
   242	    rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add]
   243	    omega
   244	  · -- same class
   245	    rw [CurveDivisor.picClass_add, CurveDivisor.picClass_divOf, mul_one]
   246	
   247	end Effective

   249	/-! ## Effective peeling of `Subsingleton H¹` -/
   250	
   251	section Peel
   252	
   253	variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
   254	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
   255	  [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
   256	
   257	/-- **Peeling one point.** Vanishing of `H¹(𝒪(B))` transports to `H¹(𝒪(B + x))` along the
   258	landed dévissage surjection `H¹(𝒪(B)) ↠ H¹(𝒪(B + x))` (`Sheaf.HModule.surjective_map_f` on
   259	`devissageSES`, whose skyscraper cokernel has vanishing `H¹`). -/
   260	lemma peel_single {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) (B : X.CurveDivisor)
   261	    (h : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K B) 1)) :
   262	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K (B + CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) 1) := by
   263	  set D : X.CurveDivisor := B + CurveDivisor.single hx 1 with hD
   264	  have hBD : devissageDivisor hx D = B := by rw [devissageDivisor_eq_sub, hD]; abel
   265	  haveI : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (devissageSES K hx D).X₃ 1) :=
   266	    skyModule_subsingleton_hModule_one x (jumpModule K hx D)
   267	  have hsurj := Sheaf.HModule.surjective_map_f (devissageSES_shortExact K hx D) 1
   268	  have hsub : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K (devissageDivisor hx D)) 1) := by
   269	    rw [hBD]; exact h
   270	  refine ⟨fun a b => ?_⟩
   271	  obtain ⟨a', rfl⟩ := hsurj a
   272	  obtain ⟨b', rfl⟩ := hsurj b
   273	  exact congrArg _ (hsub.elim a' b')
   274	
   275	/-- **Peeling a multiple of a point.** Iterating `peel_single`: `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(A))`
   276	transports to `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(A + n·x))`. -/
   277	lemma peel_nsmul_single {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) (A : X.CurveDivisor) (n : ℕ)
   278	    (h : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K A) 1)) :
   279	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K (A + n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) 1) := by
   280	  induction n with
   281	  | zero => simpa using h
   282	  | succ n ih =>
   283	    have hstep := peel_single hx (A + n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1) ih
   284	    have heq : A + n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1 + CurveDivisor.single hx 1
   285	        = A + (n + 1) • CurveDivisor.single hx 1 := by
   286	      rw [succ_nsmul]; abel
   287	    rwa [heq] at hstep
   288	
   289	/-- **Effective peeling.** Vanishing of `H¹(𝒪(A))` transports to `H¹(𝒪(A + E))` for any
   290	effective divisor `E`: peel the finitely many points of `E` one multiplicity-block at a time,
   291	by induction on the size of the support. -/
   292	lemma peel_effective (A E : X.CurveDivisor) (hE : 0 ≤ E)
   293	    (h : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K A) 1)) :
   294	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K (A + E)) 1) := by
   295	  suffices H : ∀ (n : ℕ) (E : X.CurveDivisor), 0 ≤ E →
   296	      (toFinsupp E).support.card = n →
   297	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K (A + E)) 1) from H _ E hE rfl
   298	  intro n
   299	  induction n with
   300	  | zero =>
   301	    intro E hE hc
   302	    have hE0 : E = 0 :=
   303	      Finsupp.support_eq_empty.mp (Finset.card_eq_zero.mp hc)
   304	    rw [hE0, add_zero]; exact h
   305	  | succ n ih =>
   306	    intro E hE hc
   307	    classical
   308	    have hne : (toFinsupp E).support.Nonempty := by
   309	      rw [← Finset.card_pos, hc]; exact Nat.succ_pos n
   310	    obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := hne
   311	    set b : ℤ := toFinsupp E p with hb
   312	    have hb_nonneg : 0 ≤ b := Finsupp.le_def.mp hE p
   313	    have hbpos : 0 < b := lt_of_le_of_ne hb_nonneg (Ne.symm (Finsupp.mem_support_iff.mp hp))
   314	    set E' : X.CurveDivisor := Finsupp.erase p (toFinsupp E) with hE'
   315	    have hdecomp : CurveDivisor.single p.2 b + E' = E := by
   316	      rw [hE', hb]
   317	      exact Finsupp.single_add_erase p (toFinsupp E)
   318	    have hE'nonneg : 0 ≤ E' := by
   319	      rw [hE']
   320	      refine Finsupp.le_def.mpr (fun q => ?_)
   321	      by_cases hq : q = p
   322	      · subst hq; rw [Finsupp.erase_same]; rfl
   323	      · rw [Finsupp.erase_ne hq]; exact Finsupp.le_def.mp hE q
   324	    have hcard : (toFinsupp E').support.card = n := by
   325	      have hEF : toFinsupp E' = Finsupp.erase p (toFinsupp E) := rfl
   326	      rw [hEF, Finsupp.support_erase, Finset.card_erase_of_mem hp, hc, Nat.succ_sub_one]
   327	    have hrec := ih E' hE'nonneg hcard
   328	    have hsingle : CurveDivisor.single p.2 b = b.toNat • CurveDivisor.single p.2 1 := by
   329	      rw [CurveDivisor.nsmul_single_one, Int.toNat_of_nonneg hb_nonneg]
   330	    have hsplit : A + E = (A + E') + b.toNat • CurveDivisor.single p.2 1 := by
   331	      rw [← hdecomp, ← hsingle]; abel
   332	    rw [hsplit]
   333	    exact peel_nsmul_single p.2 (A + E') b.toNat hrec
   334	
   335	end Peel

     9	# DAT-0a — the P5-uniform `H¹`-vanishing bound
    10	
    11	For the curve bundle `Y` (integral, smooth of relative dimension one, locally of finite type
    12	and quasi-compact over a field `K`) carrying a **finite dominant** morphism `π : Y ⟶ ℙ¹`,
    13	there is a single integer threshold `b`, depending only on `(Y, π)` and quantified over **all**
    14	Weil divisors `D`, past which the degree-one cohomology of `𝒪(D)` vanishes:
    15	
    16	`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1`:
    17	`∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D, b ≤ deg D → Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(D))`.
    18	
    19	This is the **P5-uniform** pre-brick of the Wave-4 datum campaign (`informal/w4-datum-worksheet.md`
    20	§2.1, §4 DAT-0a). It is consumed by DAT-D's uniform Grassmannian twist, where the twist exponent
    21	`M` is chosen so that `deg (Θ^M) ≥ b` and the whole degree-`g` family lands in the vanishing
    22	locus.
    23	
    24	## The route (worksheet §4 DAT-0a, collapsed form)
    25	
    26	The proof is the FLV-class argument (`RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean`) with the twist specialized to the
    27	fiber divisor `F = fiberWeilDivisor π` and the base twist fixed at the FLV-fiber threshold `n₁` of
    28	`D₀ = 0`:
    29	
    30	* FLV-fiber at `D₀ = 0` (`subsingleton_hModule_divisorSheaf_one_of_isFinite_toP1`) gives `n₁` with
    31	  `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(n·F))` for all `n ≥ n₁`; take `n = n₁`, so the base twist `n₁·F` is fixed;
    32	* `0 < deg F` (`zero_lt_deg_fiberWeilDivisor`) makes `b := n₁·deg F + 1 − χ(𝒪_Y)` a legal
    33	  threshold: for `deg D ≥ b` the residual class `[D]·[F]^{-n₁}` has degree `≥ 1 − χ`, so
    34	  `exists_effective_of_picClass` yields an **effective** witness `E` of that class;
    35	* `n₁·F + E` is in the class of `D`; `peel_effective` transports `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(n₁·F))` to
    36	  `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(n₁·F + E))`, and witness-independence
    37	  (`subsingleton_hModule_one_of_picClass_eq`, W6-lite) upgrades it to `𝒪(D)`.
    38	
    39	Because `n₁` (hence the base twist) is fixed, the effective witness carries the whole degree slack,
    40	and `b` depends only on `(Y, π)` — exactly the shape DAT-D consumes.
    41	-/

    84	  -- the residual class `[D] · [F]^{-n₁}`

    86	    * (CurveDivisor.picClass K (fiberWeilDivisor π) ^ n₁)⁻¹ with hc
    87	  have hcdeg : classDeg K c
    88	      = CurveDivisor.deg K D - (n₁ : ℤ) * CurveDivisor.deg K (fiberWeilDivisor π) := by
    89	    rw [hc, classDeg_mul, classDeg_inv, classDeg_pow, classDeg_picClass, classDeg_picClass]

    95	        = CurveDivisor.deg K D - (n₁ : ℤ) * CurveDivisor.deg K (fiberWeilDivisor π) := by
    96	      rw [← hcdeg, ← hWc, classDeg_picClass]
    97	    linarith

    99	  -- the witness divisor `n₁ • F + E` is in the class of `D`

   101	      = CurveDivisor.picClass K D := by
   102	    rw [CurveDivisor.picClass_add, picClass_nsmul, hEc, hWc, hc,
   103	      mul_comm (CurveDivisor.picClass K D), ← mul_assoc, mul_inv_cancel, one_mul]

   111	    peel_effective (n₁ • fiberWeilDivisor π) E hEnonneg hbase
   112	  exact subsingleton_hModule_one_of_picClass_eq K hclass hpeel

    12	# A finite morphism from the curve to the projective line
    13	
    14	For the smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible curve `C` over `k`, this file is about the
    15	existence and the basic consequences of a **finite** `k`-morphism `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹`.
    16	
    17	## Contents
    18	
    19	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite.of_locallyQuasiFinite_of_comp` — the general Zariski-main-theorem
    20	  reduction: a locally quasi-finite morphism which is proper over a separated base is finite.
    21	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite` — the specialization: a locally
    22	  quasi-finite `k`-morphism from the proper curve `C` to `ℙ¹` is finite.
    23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFinite_toP1_of_locallyQuasiFinite` — the same, in existential
    24	  form: to produce a finite `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹` over `k` it suffices to produce a locally
    25	  quasi-finite one.
    26	* Preimage bookkeeping for a finite `π`, consumed by the two-lattice finiteness argument for
    27	  `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)`: the preimages of the two standard charts are affine opens covering `C`
    28	  (`isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen`, `preimage_chartOpen_sup`), and the section ring of each
    29	  preimage is module-finite over the section ring of the chart (`finite_app_chartOpen`).
    30	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFinite_toP1` — the **existence** of a finite `π : C ⟶ ℙ¹` over
    31	  `k`, by spreading out a transcendental rational function
    32	  (`AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.RationalToP1`) and applying the reduction above; see its
    33	  docstring for the proof route.

    54	    IsFinite π :=
